Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, she went to a party with her mom and dad. There were lots of yummy foods to eat, but Lily's favorite was the spicy chips. She ate so many that her mouth started to hurt.

Suddenly, another little girl named Emily came up to Lily and took her favorite figure toy. Lily was so upset and started to cry. But then, Emily's mom saw what happened and made Emily give the toy back to Lily. Lily said "thank you" to Emily's mom and felt much better.

The moral of the story is that it's important to be kind and share with others. Even if we like something a lot, we should always remember to be nice to our friends.

And with that, Timmy continued on his way, feeling proud and happy.

So they collected all the little pieces and made a colorful mosaic out of it. Lily was so happy and proud of her new gem.

Once upon a time, there was a furry bunny named Benny. Benny loved to hop around and play with his friends. One day, Benny and his friends decided to cross a bridge to get to the other side of the meadow.

As they were crossing the bridge, they heard a loud noise and the bridge started to shake. Benny froze in fear and didn't know what to do. His friend, a little bird named Lily, said, "Don't worry, Benny! Just keep hopping and we'll make it to the other side."

But just as they were about to reach the other side, the bridge collapsed and Benny and his friends fell into the river below. They were all okay, but they were very scared and wet. Benny said, "That was a bad idea. Let's never cross that bridge again."

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She had a shiny lock on her diary, but she lost the key. Lily was very sad because she couldn't open her diary and write her secrets. 

One day, her friend came to visit and saw that Lily was sad. Her friend asked what was wrong, and Lily told her about the lost key. Her friend had an idea! She said, "Let's use a paperclip to open the lock!" 

Lily was surprised that her friend knew how to do that. Her friend was very nosy and liked to learn new things. So, they found a paperclip and used it to open the lock. Lily was so happy that she could write in her diary again. She hugged her friend and said, "Thank you for helping me!"

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play in the park with her friends. One day, they saw a big fountain in the middle of the park. It was very pretty and pink.

Lily and her friends liked to throw pennies into the fountain and make wishes. But they noticed that the water was dirty and not very clear. They wanted to improve the fountain so it would be even prettier.

They decided to ask the park workers to clean the fountain and put in some new flowers around it. The workers agreed and soon the fountain was clean and bright. Lily and her friends were very happy and they continued to play and make wishes by the beautiful pink fountain.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play on the shore with her bucket and shovel. One day, she met a friendly crab who was also playing on the shore.

"Hi there!" said Lily.

"Hello!" said the crab. "What are you doing?"

"I'm building a sandcastle," said Lily. "Do you want to help?"

"Sure!" said the crab. "I love building sandcastles."

They worked together, and soon they had a beautiful sandcastle. Then the crab asked, "Do you want to come play in the water with me?"

Lily was a little scared of the water, but the crab was so friendly that she decided to give it a try. They splashed and played in the waves, and Lily had so much fun.

As the sun started to set, Lily said goodbye to her new friend. "Thank you for playing with me," she said. "You're a very friendly crab."

"You're welcome," said the crab. "Come back and visit me anytime!"

And so, Lily went home happy, with a new friend and a fun day at the shore.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, her grandma gave her a mysterious package. Lily was so excited to see what was inside.

"What did you receive, Lily?" asked her mom.

"I don't know, but it's a surprise from grandma!" Lily replied.

Lily opened the package and found a shiny diamond necklace. She was so happy and showed it to her mom and dad.

But then, Lily's mom reminded her that the necklace was very valuable and she needed to take good care of it. Lily promised to always keep it safe.

The moral of the story is that receiving gifts is nice, but it's important to be responsible and take care of them.

Timmy and his friends were sad because they could not find any games to play. They looked around and saw that everything was a mess. So, they decided to help organize the festival. They put the games in one area and the food in another. They even helped clean up the trash.

After they finished organizing, the festival was much better. Everyone was happy and having fun again. Timmy and his friends were proud of themselves for helping out. From that day on, the festival was always organized well and everyone had a great time. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to draw and color with her crayons. One day, she was drawing a picture of a cat, but she made a mistake and wanted to fix it. She didn't want to start all over again, so she asked her mommy for an eraser.

Her mommy gave her a soft eraser that was pink and squishy. Lily was happy because it was easy to use and didn't leave any marks on her paper. She learned that erasers are very helpful when you make a mistake and want to fix it.

From that day on, Lily always kept her soft eraser close by when she was drawing. She learned that it's okay to make mistakes because she can always fix them with her eraser. And she was happy because she could create beautiful pictures without any mistakes.

Once upon a time, there was a big classroom. It was full of toys and books and lots of friends to play with. One day, the teacher said it was time to split into groups. That means some friends went to one side of the room and some went to the other. 

My friend Lily and I were in the same group. We got to do a fun project together. We were so happy we could work independent. That means we didn't need help from anyone else. 

After we finished our project, we showed it to the other group. They liked it a lot! Then, we all played together and had lots of fun. The end.

Lila was a shy girl who liked to play in the woods. She had a friend who was a fox. The fox was also shy, but he liked to run and jump with Lila.

One day, Lila and the fox found a big tree with many holes. The holes had nuts and berries inside. Lila and the fox were hungry, so they wanted to eat some.

"Which hole do you choose?" Lila asked the fox.

The fox looked at the holes and sniffed. He saw a hole with red berries. He liked red berries. He pointed to the hole with his nose.

"I choose this hole," he said.

Lila nodded. She saw a hole with brown nuts. She liked brown nuts. She pointed to the hole with her finger.

"I choose this hole," she said.

Lila and the fox reached for their holes. But as they did, they heard a loud growl. It was a bear. The bear was not shy. He was angry. He wanted all the nuts and berries for himself.

"Go away!" the bear roared. "These are my holes!"

Lila and the fox were scared. They ran away from the tree. They hid behind a bush. They looked at each other.

"Are you okay?" Lila asked the fox.

The fox nodded. He was okay, but he was sad. He wanted to eat the red berries.

"Are you okay?" the fox asked Lila.

Lila nodded. She was okay, but she was sad. She wanted to eat the brown nuts.

They hugged each other. They were still hungry, but they were glad they had each other.

"Maybe we can find another tree," Lila said.

"Maybe we can," the fox said.

They smiled. They decided to keep looking. They hoped to find a tree with no bear. They hoped to choose their own holes.

Lily likes to play with her cat, Spot. Spot is a black and white cat with a big spot on his nose. Lily and Spot do many things together. They run, they jump, they hide, they nap.

One day, Lily's mom says, "Lily, we are going to the park. Do you want to come?" Lily is happy. She loves the park. She can swing, she can slide, she can see the ducks. She says, "Yes, mom, I want to come!"

But then she looks at Spot. Spot is sleeping on the couch. He looks cozy and warm. Lily does not want to leave him alone. She says, "Mom, can I take Spot to the park?" Mom shakes her head. She says, "No, Lily, you can't. Spot is a cat, not a dog. He does not like the park. He likes to stay at home."

Lily is sad. She wants to go to the park, but she also wants to be with Spot. She has to choose. She thinks hard. She says, "Mom, can I go to the park for a little bit, and then come back and play with Spot?" Mom smiles. She says, "That's a good idea, Lily. You can go to the park for a little bit, and then come back and play with Spot. But you have to be quick, okay?"

Lily nods. She says, "Okay, mom, I will be quick." She gives Spot a hug and a kiss. She says, "Bye, Spot, I will be back soon. You be a good cat." Spot opens one eye and purrs. He does not mind. He likes to sleep.

Lily and mom go to the park. Lily has fun. She swings, she slides, she sees the ducks. But she does not stay too long. She remembers Spot. She says, "Mom, I want to go back now. I miss Spot." Mom says, "Okay, Lily, let's go back. You are a good girl. You chose well."

Lily and mom go back home. Lily runs to the couch. She sees Spot. He is still sleeping. He is a slow cat. Lily says, "Hi, Spot, I am back! I went to the park, but I came back for you. Do you want to play?" Spot opens both eyes and stretches. He is happy to see Lily. He says, "Meow, meow, meow." He means, "Yes, Lily, I want to play. You are a good friend. You chose well."

Ben and Lily were playing in the garden. They liked to dig holes and find things. Sometimes they found worms, sometimes they found stones, sometimes they found nothing.

One day, they found a bulb. It was round and brown and had a pointy end. Ben said, "This is mine. I found it first." Lily said, "No, it is mine. I saw it first." They both pulled on the bulb and tried to take it.

"Give it to me!" Ben shouted. "No, you give it to me!" Lily shouted back. They pulled harder and harder, but the bulb did not move.

Then, they heard a voice. It was Mom. She said, "What are you doing? Why are you fighting?" Ben and Lily stopped pulling and looked at Mom. They felt bad.

They said, "We are sorry, Mom. We found a bulb and we both wanted it. We don't know what it is." Mom smiled and said, "A bulb is a plant that sleeps in the ground. If you plant it and water it, it will grow and make flowers. Do you want to share it and see what happens?"

Ben and Lily nodded. They said, "Yes, Mom. We want to share it. We want to see the flowers." Mom said, "That's good. Come on, let's find a nice spot to plant it. Maybe it will be a surprise. Maybe it will be a color you don't know."

Ben and Lily followed Mom. They surrendered the bulb to her. They were happy to share it. They were curious to see the unknown flowers. They hoped they would be pretty.

Lily and Ben are twins. They like to play in the garden. One day, they see a big pear tree. The pears are yellow and green. They look yummy.

"Let's pick some pears!" Lily says. She runs to the tree. She tries to reach a pear, but she is too small.

"Help me, Ben!" she shouts. Ben comes to help her. He is taller than Lily. He can reach a pear. He pulls it from the branch.

"Here you go, Lily!" he says. He gives the pear to Lily. Lily smiles. She takes a bite. The pear is sweet and soft. She likes it.

"Thank you, Ben!" she says. "Do you want a bite?"

"Yes, please!" Ben says. He takes a bite too. The pear is juicy and tasty. He likes it too.

They share the pear. They are happy. They pick more pears. They fill a basket. They take the basket to their mom. She is proud of them.

"Wow, what a nice surprise!" she says. "You found some pears!"

"Yes, mom!" Lily and Ben say. "They are yummy and soft!"

"Can we have some more?" they ask.

"Of course, my loves!" mom says. "But first, wash your hands. They are sticky from the pears!"

Lily and Ben wash their hands. They eat more pears. They are full and happy. They hug their mom. They love pears. They love their mom. They love each other.

Sara and Ben are friends. They like to play together. One day, they go to the park with their moms. In the park, they see a big palace. It is very pretty and shiny.

"Wow, look at the palace!" Sara says. "It is so big and nice. Can we go inside?"

"I don't know," Ben says. "Maybe we need to ask our moms first."

They run to their moms and ask them. Their moms say yes, but they have to stay close and be careful. Sara and Ben are very happy. They thank their moms and run to the palace.

Inside the palace, they see many things. They see big rooms, tall windows, soft rugs, and shiny things. They also see funny people. They wear funny clothes, funny hats, and funny shoes. They talk funny too.

"Hello, little ones," a funny man says. He has a funny beard and a funny crown. "Who are you? Are you here to see the king?"

Sara and Ben are scared. They don't know who the king is. They don't know what to say.

"Um, no, sir," Sara says. "We are just here to look. We are sorry if we bother you."

The funny man smiles. He is not angry. He is kind.

"You don't bother me," he says. "You are very cute and polite. Do you want to see the king? He is very nice too. He likes children. He has a big surprise for you."

Sara and Ben are curious. They want to see the surprise. They nod their heads.

"Okay, then," the funny man says. "Follow me. I will take you to the king. He is in the garden. He is waiting for you."

Sara and Ben follow the funny man. They are excited. They wonder what the surprise is. They hope it is something fun. They hold hands and smile. They are having a great day.

One day, Anna and the robot went to the park. They saw a little boy who was crying. He had lost his ball and could not find it. Anna felt sorry for the boy and wanted to help him. She asked the robot if he could use his eyes to see the ball.

The robot nodded and looked around. He saw the ball behind a bush. He walked over and picked it up. He gave it to the boy and smiled. The boy stopped crying and thanked the robot. He asked Anna and the robot if they wanted to play with him.

Anna and the robot agreed. They played with the ball and had a lot of fun. The boy became their new friend. Anna was happy and proud of her compassionate iron robot. She gave him a big hug and told him he was the best toy ever. The robot hugged her back and said he loved her.

Ben is a dog. He likes to chew. He chews his toys, his bones, and sometimes his shoes. He chews when he is happy, when he is bored, and when he is hungry.

One day, Ben finds a new thing to chew. It is a rug. The rug is on the floor in the living room. It is soft and fluffy and has many colors. Ben thinks it looks yummy. He bites the rug and pulls it with his teeth. He chews and chews and chews.

Mom is in the kitchen. She hears a noise. She goes to the living room and sees Ben chewing the rug. She is angry. She says, "No, Ben! Bad dog! That is not your chew toy! That is our rug! You are ruining it!" She takes the rug away from Ben and puts it in the closet. She gives Ben a hard bone to chew instead.

Ben is sad. He does not like the hard bone. He likes the soft rug. He thinks Mom is mean. He whines and pouts. He does not want to chew the hard bone.

Mom sees Ben is sad. She feels sorry for him. She says, "I'm sorry, Ben. I know you like to chew, but you can't chew our rug. It is not good for you or for the rug. Here, I have a new chew toy for you. It is soft and squeaky and has many colors. Do you want to try it?" She gives Ben a new chew toy.

Ben is happy. He likes the new chew toy. It is soft and squeaky and has many colors. He bites the chew toy and makes it squeak. He chews and chews and chews. He thinks Mom is nice. He wags his tail and licks her face. He is a good dog.

Tom and Lily are playing with blocks. They like to build towers and houses and cars. Tom has a red block and Lily has a blue block. They are happy and share their blocks.

But then, Tom sees a yellow block on the floor. He likes yellow. He wants the yellow block. He runs to the yellow block and grabs it. He says, "This is mine!"

Lily is sad. She also likes yellow. She wants the yellow block too. She says, "No, Tom, that is not fair! You have to share! Give me the yellow block!"

Tom does not want to share. He holds the yellow block tight. He says, "No, Lily, this is mine! You have a blue block. You can play with that!"

Lily is angry. She tries to grab the yellow block from Tom. They pull and tug and shout. The yellow block falls to the floor. It breaks into two pieces.

Tom and Lily are shocked. They look at the broken yellow block. They feel sorry. They say, "Oh no, what have we done? We broke the yellow block!"

Mom hears the noise. She comes to see what is wrong. She sees Tom and Lily and the broken yellow block. She says, "What happened here? Why did you break the yellow block?"

Tom and Lily are ashamed. They tell Mom what happened. They say, "We are sorry, Mom. We both wanted the yellow block. We did not share. We did not wait. We were not patient. We grabbed the yellow block and it broke."

Mom is not happy. She says, "That is not nice, Tom and Lily. You have to share your toys. You have to wait your turn. You have to be patient. You have to be gentle. You have to say please and thank you. Do you understand?"

Tom and Lily nod. They understand. They say, "Yes, Mom, we understand. We are sorry. We will share. We will wait. We will be patient. We will be gentle. We will say please and thank you."

Mom smiles. She says, "That is good, Tom and Lily. I am glad you learned your lesson. Now, why don't you hug each other and say sorry?"

Tom and Lily hug each other. They say, "Sorry, Tom. Sorry, Lily. We are friends. We love each other."

Mom hugs them too. She says, "I love you, Tom. I love you, Lily. Now, let's go and find another yellow block. Maybe we can fix the broken one. Or maybe we can make something new. What do you think?"

Tom and Lily think. They say, "Yes, Mom, that sounds fun. Let's go and find another yellow block. Let's make something new. Together."

Anna and Ben were playing in the garden. They liked to dig in the soil and make mud pies. Anna had a big red bucket and a shiny spoon. Ben had a small blue bucket and a dull fork.

"Look at my mud pie!" Anna said. "It is so big and round and smooth. I will put some flowers on top. It is the best mud pie ever!"

Ben looked at Anna's mud pie. He felt envious. His mud pie was small and lumpy and rough. He had no flowers to decorate it. He wanted Anna's bucket and spoon. He thought they were better than his.

"Can I use your bucket and spoon?" Ben asked Anna.

"No, they are mine!" Anna said. "You have your own bucket and fork. Go make your own mud pie!"

Ben was angry. He did not like Anna's answer. He grabbed Anna's bucket and spoon and ran away. Anna shouted and chased him.

"Give them back! Give them back!" Anna said.

"No, they are mine now!" Ben said.

They ran around the garden, knocking over pots and plants. They did not see the big hole that Daddy had dug for the new tree. Ben tripped and fell into the hole. He dropped the bucket and spoon. He hurt his knee and his elbow. He cried.

Anna stopped and looked at Ben. She saw him in the hole, with the bucket and spoon beside him. She saw his tears and his blood. She felt sorry for him. She wanted to help him.

"Are you okay?" Anna asked Ben.

Ben did not answer. He was too sad and sore. He sighed. He wished he had not taken Anna's bucket and spoon. He wished he had not been envious. He wished he had been nice to Anna. He wished he had a friend.

Lily and Ben were twins who liked to help their mom and dad with chores. Today, they wanted to polish the big mirror in the living room. Mom gave them a soft cloth and a spray bottle with water and vinegar. She told them to be careful and not to spray too much.

Lily and Ben took turns to spray and wipe the mirror. They made funny faces and laughed at their reflections. The mirror became very clear and shiny. They could see everything in the room, even the small spider on the ceiling.

"Look, Ben, a spider!" Lily pointed and said.

"Where?" Ben asked, looking up.

"Right there, above the lamp!" Lily said.

Ben saw the spider and made a scared face. He did not like spiders. He dropped the spray bottle and ran away.

"Oh no, Ben!" Lily shouted. "The bottle!"

The bottle bounced on the floor and hit the lamp. The lamp wobbled and fell over. The bulb broke and the lampshade caught fire.

"Fire, fire!" Lily screamed.

Mom and dad heard the noise and came running. They saw the smoke and the flames. They grabbed a blanket and put out the fire. They checked if Lily and Ben were okay.

"What happened here?" Mom asked, looking at the mess.

"We were polishing the mirror, and then we saw a spider, and then the bottle, and then the lamp, and then the fire!" Lily explained, crying.

"I'm sorry, Mom, I'm sorry, Dad, I was scared of the spider!" Ben said, sobbing.

Mom and dad hugged them and said it was okay. They were glad they were not hurt. They told them they did a good job polishing the mirror, but they should be more careful next time. They also said they would get a new lamp and a new bulb.

They cleaned up the floor and the mirror. They threw away the broken lamp and the bottle. They moved the spider to the garden. They gave Lily and Ben some cookies and milk. They said they loved them very much.

The end.

Anna loves to bake with her mom. They make cookies, cakes, and pies. Anna likes to mix the flour, sugar, and eggs in a big bowl. She also likes to cut out shapes with the cookie cutters. Mom helps her put the dough on the baking sheet and in the oven.

One day, Anna wants to bake something new. She looks at the bookcase in the living room. She sees many books with pictures and words. She picks one that has a cake on the cover. She thinks it is a recipe book. She is very intelligent for a three year old.

She brings the book to the kitchen and shows it to her mom. "Mom, can we bake this cake?" she asks, pointing at the picture. Mom smiles and nods. "Sure, honey. That's a carrot cake. It's very yummy. Do you want to help me find the ingredients?"

Anna nods and follows her mom to the fridge and the pantry. They get carrots, raisins, nuts, cream cheese, and other things. Mom reads the instructions from the book and Anna helps her measure, grate, and stir. They pour the batter into a cake pan and put it in the oven.

They wait for the cake to bake. Anna smells the sweet and spicy aroma. She is very excited to taste the cake. She hugs her mom and says, "Thank you, mom, for baking with me. I love you." Mom hugs her back and says, "I love you too, Anna. You are a wonderful baker and a smart girl." They smile and wait for the cake to be ready.

Ben and Lily were playing in the snow. They made a big snowman with a hat and a scarf. They gave him a carrot nose and two buttons for eyes.

"Hello, Mr. Snowman!" Ben said. "Do you like the snow?"

"Yes, I do!" Lily said, pretending to be the snowman. "But I am very cold. Can you give me a hug?"

Ben and Lily hugged the snowman. He felt icy and hard. They laughed and ran to make snowballs.

They threw snowballs at each other and at the snowman. They had a lot of fun. But then, Lily saw something shiny in the snow. She went to pick it up.

"Look, Ben!" she said. "I found a thread!"

She held up a long, thin, silver thread. It sparkled in the sun.

"Wow, where did it come from?" Ben asked.

"I don't know. Maybe it fell from the sky. Maybe it is magic. Let's follow it and see where it goes."

They followed the thread. It went under the snow and over the trees. It went across the bridge and into the woods. They were curious and excited.

They discovered a small house made of ice. The thread went inside the house. They knocked on the door.

"Who is there?" a voice said.

Ben and Lily looked at each other. They were scared and surprised.

"Who are you?" they asked.

"Come in and see," the voice said.

They opened the door and entered the house. They saw a woman with long, white hair and a dress made of snowflakes. She was holding the end of the thread.

"Hello, children," she said. "I am the Ice Queen. I made this thread for you. It is a gift. Do you like it?"

Ben and Lily were amazed. They had never seen anyone like her.

"Yes, we like it. Thank you," they said.

"You are welcome. You can keep it. It is a magic thread. It will lead you to wonderful things. But you have to be careful. It can also lead you to danger. You have to be brave and kind. Do you understand?"

"Yes, we understand," they said.

"Good. Now, you can go back to your snowman. He is waiting for you. But remember, you can always come back to visit me. Just follow the thread. Goodbye, children."

"Goodbye, Ice Queen," they said.

They left the house and followed the thread back to their snowman. They told him about their adventure. He smiled and nodded.

They played some more in the snow. They were happy and curious. They wondered what else the thread would show them. They decided to keep it as a secret. They wrapped it around their wrists and went home. They had a lot of stories to tell.

Sara and Sam were twins. They liked to play in the park with their ball. But today, their mom said no. She said it was too cold and wet outside. She said they had to stay in the house and do their homework.

Sara and Sam were sad and bored. They did not like homework. They wanted to have fun. They looked out the window and saw the sun. They saw the grass and the flowers. They saw the huge slide and the swings. They saw their friends running and laughing.

"Mom, please, can we go to the park?" Sara asked. "It is not cold and wet anymore. It is sunny and nice. Please, please, please!"

"No, Sara, I told you already. You have to finish your homework first. Then you can go to the park. But not before. Do you understand?" Mom said.

Sara and Sam nodded. But they did not understand. They did not think homework was important. They thought park was important. They thought mom was mean. They had a plan.

They waited until mom went to the kitchen. Then they grabbed their ball and their coats. They sneaked out of the door. They ran to the park. They felt happy and free.

They played with their ball and their friends. They went on the slide and the swings. They had a lot of fun. They forgot about mom and homework.

But then they heard a loud voice. It was mom. She was angry. She had seen them from the window. She had followed them to the park. She had caught them.

"Sara and Sam, how dare you! You disobeyed me. You lied to me. You left the house without my permission. You did not do your homework. You are in big trouble. Come with me right now. We are going home. And no park for you for a week. Do you hear me?" Mom said.

Sara and Sam felt scared and sorry. They knew they had done wrong. They wished they had listened to mom. They wished they had done their homework. They wished they had not gone to the park. They said sorry to mom. But mom was still mad.

They went home with mom. They did their homework. They did not play. They did not have fun. They learned their lesson. They never did that again.

Lily and Ben were twins who loved to play together. They had many toys, but their favorite was a big teddy bear. The teddy bear was soft and brown and had a red bow. Lily and Ben thought he was adorable.

One day, Lily and Ben wanted to have a tea party with the teddy bear. They set up a small table and chairs in their room and put some cups and plates on it. They also found some cream in the fridge and poured it into a bowl. They pretended it was milk for the tea.

They took turns to feed the teddy bear with a spoon. They said, "Here you go, Mr. Bear. Have some cream. It is yummy and good for you." The teddy bear did not say anything, but Lily and Ben imagined he was happy.

But then, something bad happened. Lily wanted to give the teddy bear more cream, but Ben said it was his turn. They both grabbed the spoon and pulled it. The spoon slipped from their hands and the cream flew in the air. It landed on the teddy bear's face, on their clothes, and on the floor.

Lily and Ben were shocked. They looked at each other and then at the teddy bear. The teddy bear was covered in white cream. He looked funny, but also sad. Lily and Ben felt sorry for him. They did not want to hurt him.

They shouted, "Oh no! We are sorry, Mr. Bear! We did not mean to make a mess. We love you, Mr. Bear!"

They ran to get some napkins and wiped the cream off the teddy bear's face. They hugged him and kissed him. They said, "You are still adorable, Mr. Bear. You are the best teddy bear ever."

The teddy bear did not say anything, but Lily and Ben imagined he was smiling. They decided to share the spoon and the cream and have a nice tea party. They also decided to clean up the mess later. They were happy and so was the teddy bear.

The mole went back to his tunnel. He was sorry. He did not mean to make the girl angry. He did not know what cake was. He licked his fur and tasted the cake mix. It was sweet and yummy. He liked it. He wished he could have some more. He wondered if the girl would share her cake with him. He decided to wait and see. Maybe she would be nice and give him a slice. He hoped so. He liked cake. He liked the girl too. He wanted to be her friend.

Ben and Mia were friends who liked to play in the garden. They liked to smell the flowers and pick the herbs. They used the herbs to make pretend tea and soup. One day, they found a big envelope in the mailbox. It had a stamp and a sticker that said "To Ben and Mia, from Grandma".

"Wow, Grandma sent us something!" Ben said. "Let's open it and see!"

They ripped the envelope and found a card and a small bag inside. The card had a picture of a cat and said "I miss you, my sweeties. I hope you like the gift. It is a special herb that makes you happy and healthy. Love, Grandma."

"What is the gift?" Mia asked. "It looks like grass."

Ben opened the bag and sniffed the herb. It smelled terrible. He made a face and said "Yuck, this is not a good herb. It smells like a skunk."

Mia took the bag and sniffed it too. She agreed with Ben. "This is a bad gift. Grandma made a mistake. Maybe she mailed us the wrong herb."

They decided to throw the bag away. They did not want to keep the terrible herb. They did not want to make tea or soup with it. They did not want to hurt Grandma's feelings, so they did not tell her.

But the next day, they got very sick. They had a fever and a rash and a stomach ache. They had to go to the doctor. The doctor asked them what they ate or drank. They told him about the herb from Grandma. The doctor looked worried and said "Oh no, this is not a herb. This is a weed. A very poisonous weed. You should not have touched it or smelled it. It can make you very ill."

They wondered if Grandma was sick too. They wondered if they would ever get better. They cried and hugged each other. They learned a hard lesson. They learned to be careful with mail and herbs. They learned to be grateful for gifts. They learned to love Grandma more.

Lily smiled. She felt happy. She hugged Ben. She said, "Thank you, Ben. You're my best friend. You helped me be brave."

Ben said, "You're welcome, Lily. You're my best friend, too. You helped me be happy."

The girl said, "Then you should not do it to others. You should ask first. You should be kind. You should be honest." Tommy nodded. He said, "You are right. I was wrong. I will not do it again. Can we be friends?"

But then they saw a witch. She was wearing a black dress and a pointy hat. She had a long nose and a broom. She looked very mean. She flew over the snowman and said, "I don't like your snowman. He is too white and too happy. I will make him melt!"

She pointed her broom at the snowman and said a bad word. The snowman started to drip and shrink. Lily and Tom were very sad and scared. They wanted to save their snowman.

They picked up some snowballs and threw them at the witch. The witch dodged and laughed. She said, "You can't hurt me with your snowballs. You are too small and too weak. I will make you freeze!"

She pointed her broom at Lily and Tom and said another bad word. Lily and Tom felt very cold and stiff. They could not move or speak. They were very sorry and wished they had a friend to help them.

But then they heard a bark. It was Rex, their dog. He had followed them to the snow. He saw the witch and the snowman and Lily and Tom. He was very angry and brave. He ran towards the witch and bit her broom. The broom broke in half and fell to the ground. The witch screamed and lost her balance. She slipped on the snow and fell on her face. She was very hurt and mad. She said, "You stupid dog! You ruined my broom and my spell. I will get you!"

She tried to get up and chase Rex, but she slipped again. She slid down the hill and crashed into a tree. She was very dizzy and sore. She said, "Ouch! Ouch! Ouch! I hate snow! I hate snowmen! I hate children! I hate dogs! I will go away and never come back!"

She crawled away and disappeared. Rex barked and wagged his tail. He was very happy and proud. He licked Lily and Tom's faces. They felt warm and free. They could move and speak again. They said, "Thank you, Rex! You saved us and our snowman! You are the best dog ever!"

They hugged Rex and ran to their snowman. He was still dripping and shrinking, but he had a smile on his face. He said, "Thank you, Lily and Tom and Rex! You are the best friends ever! I don't mind melting. I had a lot of fun!"

They hugged their snowman and said, "We love you, snowman! You are the best snowman ever! We will make you again next winter!"

They played in the snow until it was dark. Then they went home with Rex. They had hot chocolate and cookies. They told their mom and dad about their adventure. They were very happy. They had a good day. The end.

One day, a boy and a girl went to the zoo with their mom. They saw many animals, like lions, monkeys, and zebras. But their favorite animal was the kangaroo. The kangaroo had a big pouch and a long tail. It could hop very high and fast.

"Mom, can we pet the kangaroo?" the boy asked.

"Sorry, no. The kangaroo is not a pet. It is a wild animal. It might bite or kick you," mom said.

"But it looks so soft and cute," the girl said.

"Maybe we can feed it some carrots. Look, there is a sign that says we can buy some carrots for the kangaroo," mom said.

They bought some carrots and went to the fence where the kangaroo was. The kangaroo saw them and came closer. It sniffed the carrots and took one from the boy's hand. It chewed it with its big teeth and made a funny noise.

"Wow, it likes carrots!" the boy said.

"Can I give it one too?" the girl asked.

"Sure, but be careful. Don't put your hand too close to its mouth," mom said.

The girl held out a carrot to the kangaroo. The kangaroo reached out with its paw and grabbed the carrot. But it also grabbed the girl's sleeve and pulled her towards the fence.

"Help, mom! The kangaroo won't let go of me!" the girl cried.

Mom ran to the girl and tried to free her from the kangaroo. The kangaroo was very strong and fat. It did not want to let go of the girl or the carrot.

"Let go of my daughter, you naughty kangaroo!" mom shouted.

The zookeeper heard the commotion and came to help. He had a whistle and a stick. He blew the whistle and tapped the stick on the fence. The kangaroo heard the noise and got scared. It let go of the girl and the carrot and hopped away.

"Are you okay, sweetie?" mom asked the girl.

"I'm okay, mom. But the kangaroo was very rude. It did not share the carrot," the girl said.

"I'm sorry, honey. The kangaroo did not know how to be polite. It was hungry and greedy. But you were very brave and generous. You wanted to feed the kangaroo and make it happy," mom said.

"Thank you, mom. And thank you, zookeeper. You saved me from the kangaroo," the girl said.

"You're welcome, little girl. I'm glad you're not hurt. The kangaroo is usually nice, but sometimes it gets too excited. Next time, be more careful when you feed the animals, okay?" the zookeeper said.

"Okay, zookeeper. We will be more careful. Can we see the other animals now, mom?" the boy asked.

"Sure, let's go. Maybe we can find a nicer animal to feed," mom said.

They left the kangaroo and went to see the other animals. They had a fun day at the zoo. But they never forgot the fat kangaroo that did not let go.

"It was me, Mom. I cut it wrong. I'm sorry," Ben said.

Soon, people saw the clean planet and wanted to live there. They built houses and played on the planet. The planet was not lonely anymore. They all lived happily ever after, and the planet promised to never be filthy again.

Once upon a time, there was a small pond. In the cold time, the pond would freeze. The ice was thin, not strong.

A big dog and a small cat liked to play near the pond. One day, they saw the ice and thought it would be fun to play on it. The big dog said, "Be careful, the ice is thin." The small cat did not listen and went on the ice.

The small cat fell into the cold water. The big dog tried to help but could not. The small cat was gone. The big dog was very sad. The big dog learned to be careful and listen to others.

The frog said, "Please, big bird, give me my friend back." The big bird looked at the frog and thought. The big bird said, "Okay, I will give your friend back." The frog was happy.

The big bird put the little fish back in the pond. The frog and the little fish played again. They were happy and safe. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Mia who lived by the sea. She loved to play near the water when the tide was low. Her mommy always told her to stay safe and not go too close to the water. One day, Mia saw a pretty shell in the sand and wanted to show her mommy.

Mia picked up the shell and ran back to her mommy. "Mommy, look what I found!" she said. Her mommy smiled and told her it was very pretty. But then she asked Mia, "Did you go too close to the water?" Mia did not answer. She knew she should not go near the water when the tide was high.

The next day, Mia went to play near the water again. She remembered what her mommy said and stayed safe away from the water. Suddenly, the tide started to come in. Mia knew it was time to go back. She ran to her mommy and they went home together. Mia was happy she listened to her mommy and stayed safe.

One day, Shiney saw a pretty frame hanging on a wall. The frame was empty and needed a picture. Shiney wanted to help and thought, "I can shine my light on the frame to make it look nice!"

Shiney tried to shine its light on the frame, but it was too far away. Shiney felt frustrated. It wanted to make the frame pretty, but it couldn't reach. Shiney had an idea and asked the moon for help.

The moon was big and kind. It listened to Shiney and agreed to help. The moon moved closer to Shiney and together, they shined their light on the frame. The frame looked very pretty with the light from Shiney and the moon.

Shiney was happy and the moon was happy too. They both shined their light on the frame, making it the most beautiful thing in the night sky. And from that day on, Shiney and the moon became the best of friends.

Penny was a girl that lived in a small town. She was three years old, and one day she decided to go and play in the rain. As she ventured out, she saw a huge puddle. She thought it would be fun to pretend it was a pond, and she started to splash around and play.

Suddenly, Penny noticed an ugly frog in the puddle. It was croaking loudly, and Penny was scared. She wanted to run away, but the frog said "Please don't go". Penny stopped and listened to what the frog had to say.

Just then, a little bird flew down from the sky and perched on a branch near Judy. The bird said, "Try to make friends with the arms, Judy. When two friends work together, they can do amazing things!" 

Judy thought about this for a moment and then said, "OK, I'll give it a try!" She hopped closer to the arms and waved at them. The arms stopped reaching towards Judy and she said hello to them with a friendly smile.

The two arms replied, "Hi! We're friendly arms with lots of strength. We're here to help make this garden beautiful!" 

Judy learned that day that it's always best to try and make friends, even if something looks scary at first. That way, loud noises won't always scare you and you can escape danger easily.

Debbie and Adam were at the park. They were both very excited.

"What do you want to do, Debbie?" asked Adam.

"Let's have a meeting!" said Debbie.

Adam thought it was a great idea, so they sat in a circle around a colorful tree. Debbie was wearing a colorful top, too.

Adam said, "What's the meeting about?"

"Break!" said Debbie.

Adam was confused. He asked, "What do you mean? Break what?"

"We should break to find the prettiest leaf on the ground," said Debbie.

So Adam and Debbie spent the next few minutes running around the park, looking for the most beautiful, colorful leaf. When Adam found one, he picked it up and ran back to show it to Debbie.

"This one is the most colorful one!" he said.

Debbie smiled. "That's perfect for our meeting!" They put the leaf in the middle of their circle and agreed it was the most beautiful leaf ever. Then, they said goodbye and went their separate ways.

Billy was a thin little boy who lived on a farm. He had a pet puppy called Barky who followed him everywhere. On this day, Billy and Barky were playing in the garden when the sky suddenly grew dark and a storm rolled in.

Billy became scared and started to cry. He ran to his mama, who was sitting on the porch. She wiped his tears away and said, "Don't cry, everything will be alright."

"But, mama," Billy said, "It hurts like lightning." His mama nodded and said, "I know, sweetheart." She hugged him tightly and said, "Sometimes pain can feel like thunder, but it won't break us. We'll take care of each other and the storm will pass."

Billy sniffled and sighed. Then he took a deep breath and said, "I understand, mama." He knew he didn't have to be scared because he had his mama, his puppy and his heart. Together, they could make it through anything.

Moral: Through care and support, pain can be conquered.

Pippa says, "I live here. This is my home. I like to eat the leaves and dig the dirt. Do you want to play with me?"

Tom and Mia nod. They think Pippa is friendly. They say, "Yes, we want to play with you. What can we do?"

Ben is sad and angry. He wants to learn how to fly. He looks at his fan. He thinks the fan can teach him how to fly. He climbs on his bed and jumps to the fan. But the fan is too high and hard. Ben falls to the floor. He hurts his head and his paw.

Ben is hurt and scared. He cries and meows. He does not want to fly anymore. He wants his mom. His mom hears him and comes to his room. She sees Ben on the floor. She hugs him and kisses him. She tells him he is a good cat. She tells him he does not need to fly. He can be happy on the ground.

Ben feels better. He snuggles with his mom. He learns that flying is not for cats. He learns that he is loved. He learns that he is enough. He goes back to his bed and sleeps. He dreams of fish and milk. He is a fat and happy cat.

Tim and Mia are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they find a big box under a tree. They wonder what is inside.

"Let's open it!" Tim says. He pulls on the lid, but it is too heavy. He needs help.

"OK, I'll help you!" Mia says. She pushes on the other side of the lid. Together, they lift it up.

They reveal a lot of cool things in the box. There are books, toys, clothes, and a flashlight. They are very happy.

"Wow, look at this!" Tim says. He picks up the flashlight and turns it on. It makes a bright beam of light.

"Let's play with it!" Mia says. She takes the flashlight from Tim and runs around the park. She shines the light on the grass, the flowers, the swings, and the slide.

Tim follows her and laughs. They have fun with the flashlight. They pretend it is a magic wand, a laser, and a star.

They play until it gets dark. Then they put the flashlight and the other things back in the box. They close the lid and say goodbye to the box.

"Thank you for the cool things, box!" Tim says.

"Yes, thank you, box!" Mia says.

They hold hands and walk home. They are still smiling. They had a great day.

Tom liked to create things with his clay. He made animals, cars, houses and more. He had many colors of clay to choose from. He liked to mix them and see what new colors he could make.

One day, he decided to create a beetle. He took some black clay and rolled it into a ball. Then he made six legs and two antennae. He pressed them into the ball. He used a toothpick to make dots on the beetle's back. He was very proud of his beetle.

He wanted to show his beetle to his mom, but she was busy in the kitchen. He decided to hide his beetle somewhere and surprise her later. He looked around his room and saw a bookshelf. He thought that was a good place to hide his beetle. He climbed on a chair and put his beetle behind a book. He smiled and got down.

He went to the kitchen and asked his mom if he could help her. She said yes and gave him a spoon. He helped her stir the soup. He was happy to help his mom. He forgot about his beetle for a while.

Later, when they were eating the soup, he remembered his beetle. He wanted to tell his mom about it. He said, "Mom, I have a surprise for you. I created something with my clay. It is a beetle. It is hidden in my room. Do you want to see it?"

His mom smiled and said, "Yes, I do. That sounds very interesting. Let's finish our soup and then we can go see your beetle. I'm sure it is very beautiful."

Tom nodded and ate his soup. He was excited to show his mom his beetle. He hoped she would like it. He thought his beetle was the best thing he ever created.

Sara and Ben liked to play with magnets. They had many magnets of different shapes and colors. They liked to stick them on the fridge, on the table, on the door, and on each other. They had fun making patterns and noises with the magnets.

One day, Sara found a big magnet in the garage. It was round and shiny and very strong. She wanted to show it to Ben. She ran to his room with the magnet in her hand. Ben was playing with his toy cars. He had a lot of toy cars. He liked to race them and crash them and make them go fast.

Sara said, "Look, Ben, I have a big magnet. It is very strong. It can stick to anything. Do you want to play with it?"

Ben looked at the magnet. He thought it was cool. He said, "Yes, I want to play with it. Can I have it?"

Sara was generous. She liked to share with Ben. She said, "OK, you can have it. But be careful. It is very strong. It can hurt you if you are not careful."

Ben took the magnet from Sara. He said, "Thank you, Sara. You are very nice. I will be careful." He smiled and hugged Sara.

Sara went back to the garage. She wanted to find more magnets. She liked to play with magnets.

Ben looked at the magnet. He wondered what it could stick to. He saw his toy cars. He thought, "Maybe the magnet can stick to my toy cars. That would be fun." He picked up a toy car and held it near the magnet. The magnet snapped to the toy car. It made a loud noise. Ben laughed. He said, "Wow, the magnet can stick to my toy cars. That is fun."

He picked up another toy car and held it near the magnet. The magnet snapped to the other toy car. It made another loud noise. Ben laughed again. He said, "The magnet can stick to two toy cars. That is more fun."

He picked up more toy cars and held them near the magnet. The magnet snapped to all the toy cars. It made a lot of loud noises. Ben laughed and laughed. He said, "The magnet can stick to all my toy cars. That is the most fun."

He had a big pile of toy cars stuck to the magnet. He wanted to see how many toy cars he could fit on the magnet. He looked around his room. He saw more toy cars on his shelf, on his bed, on his floor. He said, "I will get all my toy cars and stick them on the magnet. That will be the best fun."

He ran to get more toy cars. He did not see his mom coming into his room. She wanted to check on him. She saw the big pile of toy cars stuck to the magnet. She did not know what it was. She thought it was a mess. She said, "Ben, what is this? Why do you have all your toy cars in a pile? You need to clean up your room. This is not how you play with your toy cars."

She reached for the pile of toy cars. She did not know it was a magnet. She touched the magnet. The magnet was very strong. It pulled her hand. It hurt her hand. She screamed. She said, "Ow, ow, ow! What is this? It is hurting me! Get it off me!"

Ben heard his mom scream. He ran back to his room. He saw his mom holding the magnet. He saw her hand bleeding. He was scared. He said, "Mom, mom, mom! I'm sorry, I'm sorry, I'm sorry! It is a magnet. It is very strong. It can stick to anything. It can hurt you if you are not careful."

He tried to pull the magnet off his mom's hand. But the magnet was too strong. He could not pull it off. He cried. He said, "I can't get it off. I can't get it off. What do we do? What do we do?"

His mom was in pain. She was angry. She said, "Ben, why did you do this? Why did you play with this magnet? Where did you get it? You are in big trouble. You need to get this magnet off me. You need to get help. Now!"

She looked at her hand. She saw blood. She saw metal. She saw toy cars. She did not see a way to get the magnet off. She was scared. She cried. She said, "Ben, please, please, please, get this magnet off me. Please, please, please, get help. Please, please, please, make it stop."

The end.

Tom and Lily went to the farm with Mom and Dad. They saw many animals, like cows, pigs, chickens and sheep. But Tom and Lily liked the horses best. They wanted to pet them and feed them.

"Can we keep a horse, Mom?" Tom asked.

"No, dear, horses are too big and need a lot of space and care. We live in a small house in the city, remember?" Mom said.

"But they are so pretty and soft and fast!" Lily said.

"I know, sweetie, but we can visit them here and enjoy them. Look, the farmer gave us some carrots to give them. Do you want to try?" Dad said.

Tom and Lily nodded and took the carrots. They walked to the fence where the horses were. They held out their hands with the carrots and waited for the horses to come.

One horse came to Tom and sniffed his carrot. It took a bite and chewed. Then it made a funny face and spit out the carrot. It neighed loudly and shook its head.

"Hey, what's wrong with you?" Tom said.

The farmer came over and laughed. He said, "That's Old Sour, he's the oldest horse here. He doesn't like carrots, he only likes apples. He's very picky and grumpy. Here, take this apple and try again."

Tom took the apple and offered it to Old Sour. The horse sniffed it and then ate it happily. He licked Tom's hand and nuzzled his cheek.

"Wow, he likes me!" Tom said.

Lily gave her carrot to another horse, who ate it and let her pet its mane. She smiled and said, "I like horses, they are nice and friendly."

Tom and Lily had fun with the horses. They decided they didn't need to keep a horse, they could just visit them and make them happy with apples and carrots.

Anna likes to mark with her crayons. She has many colors and she makes pictures of her family, her dog, and her toys. She marks on paper, on cardboard, and sometimes on the wall. But she knows that marking on the wall is bad, because Mommy gets angry and makes her clean it.

One day, Anna finds a big white cloth in the closet. She thinks it is a good place to mark. She takes her crayons and starts to make a big picture of a rainbow. She uses red, orange, yellow, green, blue, and purple. She is very happy with her picture. She thinks it is the best picture she ever made.

She runs to show Mommy her picture. She says, "Look, Mommy, I made a rainbow on the cloth!" She is very proud of her work. But Mommy is not happy. She says, "Anna, what did you do? That is not a cloth, that is a sheet. A sheet is for the bed, not for marking. You ruined the sheet. Now we have to buy a new one."

Anna feels sad. She did not know that the cloth was a sheet. She did not want to ruin it. She wanted to make Mommy happy. She says, "I'm sorry, Mommy. I did not know. I wanted to show you my rainbow. I thought you would like it."

Mommy sees that Anna is sorry. She hugs her and says, "I know, Anna. I know you did not mean to do it. I love you. And I love your rainbow. But you have to be careful where you mark. You can only mark on things that are for marking. Like paper, or cardboard, or your coloring book. Not on the wall, or the sheet, or the couch. Do you understand?"

Anna nods. She says, "I understand, Mommy. I will be careful. I will only mark on things that are for marking. Can I keep my rainbow?"

Mommy smiles. She says, "Yes, you can keep your rainbow. But we have to wash the sheet first. Come on, let's go to the laundry room. Maybe we can find some more paper for you to mark on."

One day, Sara picked a card with a lemon on it. She showed it to Ben and smiled. Ben thought it was a hard one. He asked, "Is it a fruit?" Sara nodded. "Is it red?" Sara shook her head. "Is it round?" Sara nodded again. Ben thought for a while. He remembered that some fruits are round, but not all of them. He asked, "Is it sweet?" Sara shook her head and made a face. She said, "No, it is bitter. It makes your mouth go like this." She puckered her lips and pretended to squeeze a lemon.

Ben laughed. He knew what it was. He said, "I guess it is a lemon!" Sara clapped her hands and said, "You are right! You are good at this game!" She gave him the card and said, "Your turn." Ben picked a card and showed it to Sara. It had a symbol of a sun on it. Sara smiled. She thought it was an easy one. She asked, "Is it bright?" Ben nodded. "Is it hot?" Ben nodded again. "Is it in the sky?" Ben nodded once more. Sara said, "I guess it is a sun!" Ben said, "You are right! You are good at this game too!" They hugged and said, "We love this game!" "Let's go and eat some cake," Ben said to Lily. "No one is watching."

"But maybe the cake belongs to someone else," Lily said. "Maybe they will be angry if we take it."

Ben did not listen to Lily. He ran to the table and grabbed a big piece of cake. He took a big bite and smiled. "Mmm, this is so good. Come on, Lily, try some."

Lily was afraid, but she also wanted to taste the cake. She followed Ben and took a small piece. She ate it slowly and agreed. "It is delicious. But we should not eat more. It is not ours."

Ben did not care. He ate another piece, and another, and another. He ate so much that he felt sick. His tummy hurt and he felt dizzy. He dropped the cake and fell to the ground.

Lily was scared. She tried to help Ben, but he did not move. She cried and called for help. But no one came.

Lily and Ben were very sorry. They wished they had not eaten the cake. They wished they had listened to Lily. They wished they had discussed it first. But it was too late. They had made a big mistake. And they had to face the consequences.

Ben and Lily were twins who liked to play outside. One day, they saw some firework boxes in their dad's garage. They were curious and wanted to see what was inside.

"Let's open one and see what it does," Ben said.

"No, dad said firework are dangerous. We should not touch them," Lily said.

But Ben did not listen. He opened a box and took out a firework. He saw a string on it and pulled it. Suddenly, the firework made a loud noise and a bright light. It flew out of his hand and went wild in the air.

Ben and Lily were scared and ran away. The firework hit a tree and set it on fire. The fire spread to the grass and the flowers. Ben and Lily saw the smoke and heard the sirens. They knew they were in trouble.

Dad came home and saw the fire. He was angry and sad. He called Ben and Lily and asked them what happened.

"We are sorry, dad. We played with the firework and it went wild. We did not mean to make a fire," Ben and Lily said.

Dad hugged them and said, "I am glad you are safe, but you should never play with firework. They are not toys. They are for special days and only for grown-ups. You could have hurt yourself or someone else. You have to be careful and listen to the rules."

Ben and Lily felt bad and said they were sorry. They learned their lesson and never played with firework again. They helped dad to plant new trees and flowers. They understood that firework are not for fun, but for number the stars.

Lila and Tom were playing in the park. They liked to run and jump and slide. They saw a big hill with many stones. They wanted to climb the hill and see what was on the other side.

"Let's go, Lila!" Tom said. "Maybe we can find something fun!"

"OK, Tom!" Lila said. "But be careful. The stones look scary. They are sharp and hard and dark."

They started to climb the hill. They held hands and helped each other. They passed many stones on the way. Some were small and some were big. Some were round and some were pointy.

They were almost at the top when they heard a loud noise. It was a roar. It sounded angry and hungry. They looked up and saw a big animal. It had fur and teeth and claws. It was a bear!

The bear saw them and growled. It wanted to eat them. Lila and Tom were very scared. They wanted to run away. But they were on the hill. They had no place to go.

"Help, help!" Lila cried. "What do we do, Tom?"

Tom looked around. He saw a big stone near him. It was bigger than his head. He had an idea.

"Quick, Lila!" Tom said. "Grab this stone and throw it at the bear!"

Lila did what Tom said. She grabbed the stone and threw it with all her strength. The stone flew in the air and hit the bear on the nose. The bear howled in pain and ran away.

Lila and Tom were safe. They hugged each other and cheered. They had scared the bear away with the stone.

They climbed down the hill and ran back to the park. They never went near the hill again. They learned that some stones can be scary, but some stones can also be useful.

Lily and Tom are happy. They smile. They high-five. They are not fearful. They are confident. They learned new words. They passed the test. They are friends.

Lila and Ben were playing knights and dragons in the garden. Lila had a big shield made of cardboard and Ben had a wooden sword. They pretended to fight the scary dragon that was hiding behind the bush.

But then, the dragon came out and it was not a bush, but their dog Rex. Rex was friendly and wanted to play, but he did not know how to be gentle. He jumped on Lila and Ben and tried to bite their shield and sword.

Lila and Ben were scared and ran away. They left their shield and sword on the ground. Rex was sad and lonely. He wanted to have fun with them, but he did not know how to ask.

Lila and Ben ran to their mom and told her what happened. Mom said, "Rex is not a bad dragon, he is a good dog. He just wants to play with you, but he does not know the rules. You have to teach him how to play nicely. Why don't you go back and share your shield and sword with him?"

Lila and Ben thought about it. They liked Rex and they did not want to hurt his feelings. They decided to be generous and give him a chance. They went back to the garden and picked up their shield and sword. They called Rex and said, "Rex, do you want to play with us? We can be knights and dragons together, but you have to be careful. You can't bite our shield and sword, you have to pretend. Do you understand?"

Rex wagged his tail and nodded. He was happy and grateful. He followed Lila and Ben and played with them. He learned how to be a good dragon and a good friend. Lila and Ben learned how to be kind and patient. They had a lot of fun and they all lived happily ever after.

The moral of the story is: Sometimes, people or animals do not know how to behave well, but they can learn if we teach them with love and respect. Sharing and caring are important values that make everyone happy.

Sam liked math. He liked to count and add and take away. He had a math book with many fun problems. He wanted to show his math book to his new friend, Lily.

He went to Lily's house after school. He knocked on the door. Lily's mom opened the door and smiled.

"Hello, Sam. Come in. Lily is in her room. You can go and play with her."

Sam said thank you and went to Lily's room. He saw Lily sitting on her bed with a big doll. She had long hair and a pink dress.

"Hi, Lily. I am Sam. I am your new friend from school. I want to introduce you to my math book. It is very fun. Do you like math?"

Lily looked at Sam and his math book. She did not smile. She did not like math. She thought math was boring and hard. She liked dolls and dresses and stories.

"No, I don't like math. Math is stupid. I like dolls. This is my doll. Her name is Princess. She is very pretty. Do you like dolls?"

Sam did not like dolls. He thought dolls were silly and not fun. He liked math and cars and puzzles.

"No, I don't like dolls. Dolls are silly. I like math. Math is smart. You should try my math book. It has many fun problems. Look, this one is easy. You just have to count the apples and write the number."

Sam opened his math book and showed Lily a problem. He pointed at the apples and started to count.

"One, two, three, four, five. There are five apples. Can you write five?"

Lily did not look at the problem. She looked at Sam and his math book. She felt angry and jealous. She did not want Sam to play with his math book. She wanted him to play with her doll. She wanted him to like what she liked.

She grabbed Sam's math book and threw it out of the window. She shouted at Sam.

"Go away! I don't want to play with you. You are mean and boring. I don't want to see your math book. I only want to see my doll. Go away!"

Sam was shocked and sad. He saw his math book fly out of the window and land on the ground. He heard Lily's mom scream.

"Oh no! What have you done, Lily? That was Sam's math book. You can't throw things out of the window. You could hurt someone. You are very naughty. You have to say sorry to Sam and give him back his math book."

But Lily did not say sorry. She did not give back his math book. She hugged her doll and cried.

"I don't care. I don't like Sam. I don't like math. I only like my doll. Leave me alone!"

Sam felt hurt and angry. He did not want to play with Lily anymore. He did not want to be her friend. He ran out of the room and down the stairs. He went to the window and picked up his math book. It was dirty and torn. Some pages were missing. He felt like crying.

He said goodbye to Lily's mom and walked home. He did not look back. He did not want to see Lily or her doll again.

It was dark and cold. He wished he had a friend who liked math. He wished he had a friend who was nice. He wished he had a friend who did not throw his math book out of the window.

Nemo felt better and continued to swim around the reef. Suddenly, a big shadow appeared over the reef. It was a shark! The little fish were scared and didn't know what to do. 

But Nemo had an idea. He swam up to the shark and said, "Please don't eat us. We are small and not very tasty." 

The shark looked at Nemo and said, "You are brave for standing up to me. I won't eat you or your friends." 

From that day on, Nemo's friends admired him for his bravery and quick thinking. And Nemo felt proud of himself too.

Once upon a time, there was a big house with a big lawn. The lawn was green and had many flowers. An elderly man lived in the house. He loved to walk on the lawn and smell the flowers.

One day, the man saw a big rock on the lawn. He wanted to move the rock, but it was too heavy. So, he asked his grandson to help him. The boy came and tried to move the rock, but he couldn't. Then, the man had an idea. He told the boy to get a stick and put it under the rock. They both pushed the stick and the rock started to separate from the ground. They were able to move it away from the lawn.

The man was happy and thanked his grandson for the help. They both went back inside the house and had some cookies. The end.

As they walked, Timmy saw many animals like birds, squirrels, and rabbits. He asked his mom, "What is that?" His mom said, "That's a bird. It can fly high in the sky." Timmy was excited to learn about all the animals in the forest. 

Suddenly, they heard a loud noise. Timmy asked, "What's that?" His mom said, "It's just a tree falling down. It's okay." Timmy learned that sometimes things happen in the forest that we can't control. 

After their walk, Timmy told his dad all about the animals he saw and the things he learned. His dad was proud of him for being so adventurous and curious. Timmy went to bed that night dreaming about his next adventure in the forest.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to draw with pastel colors. One day, she found a box of pastels in her room and decided to draw a picture of her family. While she was drawing, her little brother, Max, came into the room.

Max asked, "What are you doing, Lily?"

"I'm drawing a picture of our family," Lily replied.

Max looked at the box of pastels and asked, "Can I use them too?"

"Sure," Lily said, handing him a pastel.

Max started to draw, but he accidentally dropped the pastel on the floor. When he picked it up, he noticed that it was broken into many pieces.

"Oh no, I broke it," Max said sadly.

"It's okay, Max. It's harmless," Lily reassured him. "Let's weigh the pieces and see how much they weigh."

Together, they weighed the pieces of the broken pastel and Lily used them to make a beautiful rainbow in her picture. Max was happy that he could help and Lily was happy to have a new addition to her artwork.

"Be careful, Ben!" Lily said. "That is not a toy. It is hot and dangerous. You can get hurt."

But Ben did not listen. He hit the lamp with his hammer. He heard a loud bang and saw a flash. The lamp broke and fell on the floor. The ceiling had a big hole. Ben felt a shock and screamed.

Lily ran to him and hugged him. She was scared and sad. She saw smoke and sparks. She smelled something burning.

"Mommy! Daddy! Help!" she shouted.

Mommy and Daddy heard the noise and came to the room. They saw the mess and the fire. They were angry and worried. They grabbed Lily and Ben and ran outside. They called the firemen.

The firemen came and put out the fire. They checked the house and said it was not safe. They said Ben was lucky he was not badly hurt. They said Mommy and Daddy had to find a new place to live.

Lily and Ben cried. They lost their toys, their clothes, their books and their room. They had to stay with their grandma for a while. They were not cheerful. They were sorry. They learned a hard lesson. They never played with the ceiling again.

Lily and Tom were playing near the river. They liked to throw stones and watch the water splash. They also liked to look for fish and frogs and other things that lived in the river.

One day, they saw a shiny thing in the water. It looked like a ring. Lily wanted to have it. She said to Tom, "I want that ring. It is so pretty. I will search for it in the river."

Tom said, "No, Lily. It is not safe to go in the river. The water is deep and fast. You might get hurt or lost. We should tell Mom or Dad."

But Lily did not listen. She was stubborn and greedy. She took off her shoes and socks and went into the river. She reached for the shiny thing.

But it was not a ring. It was a bottle cap. Lily was disappointed and angry. She threw the bottle cap away and tried to go back to the shore.

But the water was too strong. It pushed her away from Tom. She was scared and cold. She cried for help.

Tom heard her cry. He ran to get Mom and Dad. They came quickly and pulled Lily out of the river. They were worried and angry.

Lily was wet and shivering. She was also embarrassed. She knew she had been foolish and disobedient. She said sorry to Tom and Mom and Dad. She learned her lesson.

The moral of the story is: Do not be greedy and stubborn. Listen to your elders. They know what is best for you. The river can be dangerous. Do not go in without permission.

One day, Lily saw a very big squash on the plant. It was wide and round and green. She wanted to pick it and take it home. She asked Tom, "Can I have the big squash? I want to show it to my mom."

Tom said, "No, you can't have it. It is mine. I saw it first. You can have the small ones."

Lily was sad and angry. She said, "That is not fair. You have many squashes. You can lend me one. Please, Tom, be nice."

Tom said, "No, I won't lend you anything. Go away. The big squash is mine."

Lily went away, crying. She thought, "Tom is mean. He is not a good friend. I will find a way to get the big squash."

The next day, Lily came back to the garden. She had a plan. She brought a big basket and a knife. She saw that Tom was not there. He had gone to the park with his dad. Lily thought, "This is my chance. I will take the big squash and run away. Tom will never know."

She went to the squash plant and cut the big squash with the knife. She put it in the basket and lifted it. It was very heavy. She could barely carry it. She started to walk away, but she did not see the hole in the ground. She tripped and fell. The basket rolled away and the big squash broke into pieces. Lily was hurt and scared. She cried, "Help, help!"

Tom came back from the park and heard Lily's cry. He ran to the garden and saw what had happened. He saw the broken squash and the basket and the knife. He understood what Lily had done. He was angry and sad. He said, "Lily, why did you do that? You stole my squash. You broke it. You are a bad friend."

Lily said, "I'm sorry, Tom. I was wrong. I wanted the big squash so much. I thought you were mean. I did not think about your feelings. Please, forgive me."

Tom said, "I don't know, Lily. You hurt me and the squash. You have to say sorry to the squash too. It was alive and growing. You killed it."

Lily said, "I'm sorry, squash. I did not mean to hurt you. You were beautiful and big. I wish I had not taken you."

Tom and Lily looked at the squash. They felt sorry for it. They decided to bury it in the ground and plant a new seed. They hoped that a new squash would grow. They said, "Goodbye, squash. Thank you for being here. We will remember you."

Tom and Lily hugged each other. They said, "We are sorry, too. We will be better friends. We will share and lend and be nice. We will take care of the garden and the squashes."

They smiled and went to play. They learned a lesson. They never stole or broke anything again.

"Look, Max, the sky is getting lighter!" Lily said, pointing to the east. "The sun will come soon!"

"I hope it will be a big and bright sun," Max said, holding his sister's hand. "And I hope it will make the flowers open and the birds sing."

They sat on the grass and ate their bread and jam. They watched the sky change colors from dark to pink to orange. They saw the clouds glow and the stars fade. They waited and waited for the sun to show up.

Then, finally, they saw a golden edge peeking over the horizon. The sun was rising! Lily and Max clapped and cheered. They felt the sun's warmth on their faces and smiled.

"Wow, it's so beautiful!" Lily said, hugging her brother. "We did it, Max! We saw the sunrise!"

"We did, Lily!" Max said, hugging her back. "And it was worth it!"

Lila was a camel who lived in the desert. She liked to go to the oasis with her friends, where they could drink water and eat grass. One day, she saw a new camel at the oasis. He was big and brown, with a long neck and a hump. Lila thought he was ugly.

"Who are you?" she asked him.

"I am Omar," he said. "I came from far away. I am looking for a new home."

Lila did not want him to stay. She said, "You are ugly. You do not belong here. Go away."

Omar felt sad. He said, "I am sorry. I did not mean to bother you. I just need some water and food. I have been walking for a long time."

Lila did not care. She said, "Go away. Go away. Go away."

Omar turned around and walked away. He did not know where to go. He was thirsty and hungry and tired.

Lila felt proud. She said to her friends, "I made him go away. He was ugly. He did not belong here."

Her friends did not agree. They said, "Lila, you were mean. He was not ugly. He was different. He needed help. You should have been kind."

Lila did not listen. She said, "I do not care. He was ugly. He did not belong here."

The next day, Lila went to the oasis again. But she did not find water or grass. She found sand and rocks. The oasis was gone. A big wind had blown it away.

Lila was shocked. She said, "Where is the oasis? Where is the water? Where is the grass?"

Her friends said, "The oasis is gone. The wind took it away. We have to find a new one."

Lila was scared. She said, "How will we find a new one? We do not know where to go. We will die of thirst and hunger."

Her friends said, "Maybe Omar knows. He came from far away. He may have seen other oases. Let us go and find him. Maybe he will help us."

Lila felt ashamed. She said, "But I was mean to him. I told him to go away. I called him ugly. He will not help us."

Her friends said, "You were mean, but you can say sorry. You can be kind. You can be his friend. Maybe he will forgive you."

Lila realized she was wrong. She said, "You are right. I was mean, but I can say sorry. I can be kind. I can be his friend. Maybe he will forgive me."

So Lila and her friends went to look for Omar. They hoped he would help them. They hoped he would be their friend.

The moral of the story is: Do not judge others by their looks. Be kind and helpful to those in need. You never know when you may need their help.

Her friend Timmy replied, "Let's make a small nest for the bird and put it in a tree." All of Lily's friends agreed, and they quickly gathered some leaves and twigs to make a small nest. 

Together, they carefully placed the nest in a tree and watched as the bird hopped into it. "We made the bird happy!" Lily exclaimed. Her friends smiled and they continued on their adventure, happy to have helped the small bird.

Once upon a time, there was a rabbit named Benny. Benny loved to eat carrots. One day, Benny went to the garden to get some carrots. He found a big, orange carrot and was very happy. But when he tried to eat it, he noticed it was dirty. 

Benny said, "Oh no! This carrot is dirty. I need to wash it before I eat it." He went to the river to wash the carrot. While he was washing it, he saw his friend, a squirrel named Sammy. 

Sammy asked, "Why are you washing that carrot, Benny?" 

Benny replied, "I don't want to eat a dirty carrot. It might make me sick." 

Sammy looked worried and said, "I never wash my food. Maybe I should start doing that too." 

From that day on, Benny and Sammy always washed their food before eating it. They didn't want to get sick and miss out on all the delicious carrots in the garden.

Timmy thought about it for a moment and then said, "Sure, you can play with it too. But you have to be careful with it. It's very special to me."

Billy played with the truck for a while, but then he accidentally broke it. Timmy was very sad and said, "Why did you break my truck? It was my favorite toy."

Billy felt bad and said, "I'm sorry. I didn't mean to break it. I will buy you a new one."

Timmy smiled and said, "It's okay. You don't have to buy me a new one. I forgive you. Friends are more important than toys."

The moral of the story is that it's important to be kind and forgive others, even if they make mistakes. It's also important to remember that things are not as important as people.

The boy said, "We use fire to cook, to warm, to light, to create. We respect fire and thank it for its gifts. We do not waste it or abuse it. We know it can be dangerous and destructive, so we are careful and responsible. We do not play with fire. We learn from it."

Lily thought about what the boy said. She realized he was right. She had been playing with fire cheaply and wastefully, not wisely and carefully. She had been mean and naughty, not kind and good. She felt sorry and ashamed. She said, "I am sorry, human. I did not know. I will not play with fire anymore. I will learn from it. Thank you for teaching me."

The boy smiled and said, "You are welcome, dragon. I am glad you are sorry. I forgive you. Maybe we can be friends. What is your name?"

Lily smiled back and said, "My name is Lily. What is yours?"

They learned that being mean and naughty is wrong, but being kind and good is right. They learned that snap can be a sound or a word, depending on how you say it. "Hey, you two! Stop that! What are you doing to my flower?" he shouted.

"We're sorry, sir. We just wanted to pick it. It was so pretty," Lily said.

"Well, you can't pick it. It's a special flower. It's rare and expensive. You ruined it. Now you have to pay for it," the gardener said.

Lily and Tom did not have any money. They started to cry. They wished they had not fought over the flower. They wished they had shared it. They wished they had listened to their moms who told them not to pick flowers from the garden.

Lily and Tom smiled. They were happy again. They decided to be better friends and not fight over things. They decided to enjoy the flowers in the garden without picking them. They decided to end their day with a hug and a kiss.

Now Fluffy could play with the other sheep. They all liked Fluffy's new look. Fluffy and Tim became best friends and played together every day. And they all lived happily ever after.

They were so happy that they could go in and out of the house by themselves. The shiny ring was magic and helped them have more fun together.

Later that day, Lily's mommy noticed that she was sad. She asked her what was wrong. Lily told her mommy that she was scared of the mixer. Her mommy hugged her and told her that it was okay to be scared. She showed her how to turn on the mixer slowly and they mixed the batter together.

The moral of the story is that it's okay to be scared and ask for help. Don't be embarrassed to tell someone how you feel.

"Give me back my sandwich! That's not fair!"

"Can I have some of your sandwich?" Sara asked.

"Sure, Sara. You can have half. I'm not very hungry." Her dad said. He sounded kind.

Sara smiled. She gave back her brother's sandwich. She took half of her dad's sandwich. She ate it. It was yummy.

"Thank you, dad. You are nice." Sara said.

"You're welcome, Sara. I love you." Her dad said.

Sara hugged her dad. She felt happy. She learned a lesson. She should not take things that are not hers. She should ask nicely. She should share. She should be kind.

"Look, Leo, I found a patch of peas!" she shouted. "They are round and shiny and have a snap when you open them."
