"Mmm, delicious!" he said. "Can we eat more?"

Mia nodded and snapped another pod. She ate some peas and gave some to Leo. They enjoyed the sweet and crunchy snack.

"Let's take some to Mommy and Daddy," Mia said. "Maybe they will like them too."

They filled their pockets with pea pods and ran to the house. They showed their parents what they had found and offered them some peas.

"Wow, what a nice surprise!" Mommy said. "You found a patch of peas in the garden. They are delicious indeed. Thank you for sharing them with us."

"You're welcome, Mommy," Mia and Leo said. "We like to find things in the garden. Can we go back and play some more?"

"Of course, you can," Daddy said. "But be careful not to snap all the peas. Leave some for the plants to grow."

"OK, Daddy," Mia and Leo said. "We will leave some for the plants. And maybe for the bugs too."

They hugged their parents and ran back to the garden. They had fun playing and snapping and eating and sharing. They loved their patch of peas.

Once there was a furry bear who lived deep in a dark forest. He had a special stick that he kept safe near his cozy den. One day, it started to rain and the bear decided to go play in the rain.

He held his stick tight, and ran around in circles, spinning and jumping and smiling. But then, he slipped on a slippery log and fell down into a little mud puddle.

The bear was sad. He tried really hard to lift the stick to get up, but it was too heavy. He waited, being very patient.

Finally, a little squirrel came out of a nearby tree. He noticed the bear struggling, so he jumped over and grabbed the bottom of the stick. He used all of his strength to help the bear pull the stick, until finally the bear was out of the mud.

The bear thanked him with a big bear hug, and the squirrel showed him something special. He had a sharp rock, and scratched it against the stick to make it even more special. The bear liked his new stick and thanked the squirrel for being so helpful and patient.

Ever since that day the bear carries his stick everywhere, and it serves as a reminder of his special friend who helped him that rainy day.

One day, Max and his mommy were walking in the park. Max was looking around curiously, as he was very enthusiastic to discover new things. Suddenly, Max noticed something that made him jump. It was a mosquito with buzzing wings!

Max's mommy chuckled and said, "That's a mosquito, Max. Don't be scared." Max looked up and asked, "What is mosquito?" 

"Well," said Mommy, "mosquitoes are insects, which means very small creatures. You can usually find them near water, and they love to bite people."

Max was confused and asked, "What can someone do if a mosquito bites them?"

"Well, first you have to learn about mosquitoes and how to protect yourself from them," said Mommy, sternly. "That's why you should study them and make sure you're safe. Understand?"

Max nodded and said, "Yes, Mommy."

Max and his mommy continued their walk in the park, but now Max was looking at the mosquitos with a different, more enthusiastic attitude. He wanted to learn more about them, so he could protect himself.

"Ow, ow, ow! My hand hurts!" she cries.

"Oh, Sara, I'm so sorry. You hurt your hand. Let me see," she says.

"There, there. It will be better soon. You are very brave, Sara," she says.

Sara stops crying and smiles a little. She sees her paper on the floor. It is wrinkled and torn.

"Mom, look. My design is ruined. I worked so hard on it," she says.

Sara looks at the paper and sees her handprint. She sees that it is the same shape and size as her hand. She feels happy and proud again.

"Really, mom? It is still pretty? It is special?" she asks.

"Yes, Sara, it is. It is a beautiful design, and it is yours. You can hang it on the wall, or give it to someone you love. They will love it too, because it is from you," mom says.

"What is going on here?" she asks.

"Anna and Ben, you need to share and be nice to each other. Fighting over toast is not good. You can have more toast if you ask politely. Or you can have something else, like fruit or yogurt. But you have to yield and say sorry first."

Anna and Ben look at each other. They feel bad for fighting. They do not want to make their mom sad.

"Sorry, Anna," Ben says.

Jill and Jack were twins who liked to play with their baby brother Tom. They loved to hug him, kiss him, and make him laugh. Sometimes, they also liked to help their mom with the chores, like folding the clothes.

One day, mom asked them to fold the towels and put them in the closet. Jill and Jack were eager to show how good they were. They ran to the laundry basket and grabbed the towels. They tried to fold them neatly, but they were too big and heavy for their small hands.

"Let's ask Tom to help us," Jill said. "He can hold one end of the towel while we fold the other."

"Good idea," Jack said. "He will have fun too."

They carried a towel to Tom, who was sitting on the floor with his toys. They put one end of the towel in his hands and smiled at him.

"Tom, can you help us fold the towel?" Jill asked. "It's easy. Just hold it tight and don't let go."

Tom looked at the towel and giggled. He liked the soft and fluffy feeling. He held it with his fingers and pulled it towards his mouth.

"No, Tom, don't do that!" Jack shouted. "You will make it dirty and wet. You have to fold it, not eat it."

But Tom didn't listen. He kept chewing on the towel and making funny noises. Jill and Jack tried to take it away from him, but he was stronger than they thought. He held on to the towel and cried.

"Mom, mom, help us!" Jill and Jack called. "Tom won't let go of the towel. He's ruining it."

Mom heard their cries and came to see what was wrong. She saw Tom with the towel in his mouth and Jill and Jack pulling on the other end. She was angry and sad.

"What are you doing?" she asked. "Why did you give Tom a towel to play with? He's a baby, he doesn't know how to fold. He could choke on it or get sick. You should have left him alone with his toys. You were not helping, you were making trouble."

She took the towel from Tom and checked if he was okay. She scolded Jill and Jack and told them to go to their room. They felt sorry and ashamed. They realized they had made a mistake. They wished they had listened to mom and not bothered Tom.

The moral of the story is: Don't give tasks to someone who is not ready for them. You might cause harm instead of help.

Sam decided he would not act like a mouse. He would act like a lion. He would roar and jump and scare everyone. He thought that would be funny and make him the star of the play. He did not care what the teacher or the other kids said. He only cared about himself.

The day of the play came. Sam put on his newspaper costume and waited for his cue. When he saw the lion on the stage, he ran towards him, not away from him. He roared and scratched and bit the lion's tail. The lion was surprised and hurt. He cried out and ran off the stage. The other animals were confused and scared. They did not know what to do. The teacher was angry and stopped the play. She scolded Sam and sent him to the corner. The audience was disappointed and booed. Sam felt ashamed and sorry. He realized he had ruined the play and hurt his friend. He wished he had acted like a mouse, not like a lion.

The moral of the story is: Be happy with who you are and respect others. Don't try to be someone you're not and ruin things for everyone. Acting is fun, but only when you follow the rules and work with your team.

The girl tried to help the cow, so she threw a rope around the cow and pulled her to the top of the hill. She said, "Come on cow, let's keep walking!" The cow kept chewing and eating, and slowly the weight began to go away. 

The cow and the girl walked for a long time. Finally, when the cow reached the top of the hill, she felt like a different cow. She was so happy and full of energy! She was no longer fat and heavy and she could chew her food with ease. She thanked the little girl for all her help, then went off to find some more yummy things to eat. 

The end.

The two frogs got ready and began their race. The big frog was going very fast, but the small frog was determined to keep up. In the end, the small frog amazed the crowd by crossing the pond first. The rubber duck decided to start its own adventure. He started to walk and before long he was walking so far that he was completely lost. Then, he spotted a large mountain in the distance. So, he began to climb the mountain, but it was so tall that he almost stopped.

Finally, the rubber duck made it to the top and could finally see his friends swimming in the lake below. He wanted to join them, so he took a large leap off the mountain and landed right in the middle of the lake. His friends were so excited to see him that they all swam over to say hello.

The rubber duck had solved his mystery. He had found his lost friends. And now, the large rubber duck and his duck friends were never apart again.

The little girl felt so safe and content in the old place. She loved the song that repeated again and again, so she sang along. Everywhere she went, she heard the repeating song and it made her feel so calm. 

The little girl wanted to stay in the old place forever, but soon it was time to go home. She said goodbye with a heavy heart, but she knew she would be back soon. She would always remember the happy old place with the repeating song.

Once there was a little girl. She enjoyed watching the butterfly in her garden every day, but one day was different. She looked up at the butterfly, but as it fluttered around, she started feeling dizzy. She didn't like it and started to hate the butterfly.

The little girl screamed and waved her arms at the butterfly. She wanted the butterfly to go away, but it wouldn't listen. The dizzy feelings were still there, and they were getting worse.

The little girl tried running and even hiding, but the butterfly was still there and the dizzy feeling stayed with her. She started to cry because she hated the butterfly so much.

So, the little girl decided to stay away from the garden, and never looked at the butterfly again. This made her feel better, but the dizzy feeling still stayed with her when she went outside.

The end.

Once upon a time there was an adorable bunny, called Fluffy. Fluffy had an amazing notebook that he kept with him all the time, because it was special. One day while he was hopping around, Fluffy spotted something he had never seen before between the grass and the trees. He hopped towards it, but it was so unusual that he couldn't recognize what it was.

When Fluffy got closer, he noticed a strange creature that he had never seen before. It had a kind face, and it smiled at him. Fluffy was very curious about the creature, and he wanted to know who it was, but he still couldn't recognize it.

Suddenly, Fluffy realised the creature was his reflection, in the mirror-like water of the pond. Fluffy was happy that day, because he had learned something new and important: he had finally recognized himself as unique and special.

The moral of the story is: be proud of who you are and recognize your own strengths and uniqueness.

Later, the prince saw everyone eating the green slimy food and having fun. He felt sad and regret not trying it. The prince decided to be brave and try the disgusting food. To his surprise, it was yummy! The prince learned to not judge food by how it looks.

Once upon a time, in a small country, there lived a sad duck. The duck was sad because he was very dirty. He wanted to bathe and be clean like the other ducks.

One day, the sad duck saw a pond. He was so happy to find a place to bathe. He jumped into the pond and started to clean himself. The other ducks saw him and came to join him too.

But the pond was not safe. A big, mean fish lived in the pond. The fish saw the ducks and wanted to eat them. The sad duck tried to swim away, but the fish caught him. The other ducks were scared and flew away.

The big, mean fish ate the sad duck. The other ducks never went back to that pond again. They found a new, safe place to bathe and be clean. But they always remembered the sad duck and missed him very much.

As they continued their walk, they saw a man brushing his horse. Lily asked the man, "Can I brush your horse too?" The man smiled and said, "Sure, you can jump up on the stool and brush him." Lily was so excited and jumped up on the stool. She brushed the horse's mane and tail, feeling very proud. 

After they finished brushing the horse, Lily and Max went back home. Lily showed her mom the lucky penny and told her all about brushing the horse. Her mom said, "You're so lucky to have such a fun day with Max and the horse." Lily smiled and felt very happy.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She lived in a big house with her family. One day, her mom told her to clean her room. Lily didn't like cleaning, but she did it anyway. She used a broom to sweep the dust off the floor. 

Later that night, Lily went to bed. She was very comfortable under her soft blanket. Suddenly, she heard a strange noise coming from under her bed. She was scared, but she remembered her mom telling her to be brave. 

Lily slowly peeked under her bed and saw a tiny mouse. The mouse looked scared too. Lily remembered how she swept the dust earlier and realized that the mouse must have been living under her bed in the dust. She felt bad for the mouse and decided to make a little bed for it with some of her old clothes. 

From that day on, Lily and the mouse became good friends. She would hear it scurrying around at night, but she no longer felt scared. She was happy to have a new friend and to have made her bed a little more comfortable for both of them.

From that day on, Jack knew that it was important to stand up for his friends. He learned that sometimes, you have to fight to protect the people you care about. And even though he was just a youth, Jack knew that he could make a difference in the world.

Lily's mom took her back to the doctor, but this time the news was not good. The doctor said that Lily's leg was not fit to run and play anymore. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the garden with her toys. One day, she saw a worm in the soil. 

"Hello little worm, what are you doing in the soil?" asked Lily.

"I am eating the soil, it is very fine and delicious," replied the worm.

Lily was surprised to hear that the worm liked to eat soil. "Doesn't it rot your tummy?" she asked.

"No, it doesn't rot my tummy. I like to eat soil because it helps me grow big and strong," said the worm.

Lily was happy to learn something new about the worm and the soil. She continued to play outside in the garden, knowing that the soil was important for all the plants and animals to grow big and strong.

"Let's lay the melon on the grass and roll it," Sara said. "Maybe it will break open and we can eat it."

"OK," Ben said. They laid the melon on the grass and pushed it with their hands. The melon rolled and rolled, but it did not break.

"Let's roll it harder," Ben said. He pushed the melon with all his strength. The melon rolled faster and faster, until it hit a rock and bounced off. It flew in the air and landed on the fence, where a bird was sitting.

"Look out, bird!" Sara shouted. The bird was scared and flew away. The melon fell from the fence and smashed on the ground. The juice and seeds splashed everywhere.

"Oh no, our melon!" Ben cried. He ran to the melon and picked up a piece. It was sweet and juicy, but there was not much left.

"Sorry, bird," Sara said. She saw the bird on a tree, looking sad. She picked up another piece of melon and walked to the tree. She held out the melon to the bird. "Do you want some melon, bird? We did not mean to scare you."

The bird looked at Sara and the melon. It saw that Sara was gentle and kind. It flew down and took the melon from Sara's hand. It ate the melon and chirped happily.

"Thank you, bird," Sara said. She smiled and petted the bird. The bird liked Sara and stayed on her shoulder.

"Can I pet the bird, too?" Ben asked. He came to Sara and the bird with his piece of melon.

"Sure," Sara said. "But be gentle, OK?"

"OK," Ben said. He was gentle and careful. He petted the bird and gave it some melon. The bird liked Ben, too, and hopped on his shoulder.

Sara and Ben were happy. They had made a new friend. They shared the rest of the melon with the bird and each other. They did not mind that the melon was broken. They had learned that sharing and being gentle were more important.

"Maybe he was just an old trickster who fooled us all," their mom said.

Lily and Ben still did not listen. They added more blocks to their castle. It was almost done. They were proud of their work.

But then, something bad happened. The cat jumped on the couch and saw the castle. He thought it was a toy. He ran towards it and pounced on it. He knocked down all the blocks and made a big mess.

Lily and Ben cried. They were sad and angry. They had worked hard on their castle and the cat ruined it.

"Bad cat!" Lily shouted. "Go away!"

"Meow!" The cat said. He did not care. He liked to play with the blocks.

Mom came to the living room and saw what happened. She hugged Lily and Ben and comforted them.

"I'm sorry, kids," she said. "The cat did not know. He was just curious. But you should have listened to me and come for lunch. Maybe you could have prevented this from happening."

Lily and Ben nodded. They realized they were wrong. They should have obeyed Mom. They were also hungry. They had not eaten for a long time.

"Can we still have lunch, Mom?" Ben asked.

"Of course, honey," Mom said. "But first, let's clean up this mess. And then, we can eat. It will only take a minute."

Lily and Ben agreed. They helped Mom pick up the blocks and put them away. They washed their hands and sat at the table. They ate their sandwiches and fruits and drank their milk. They felt better.

"Can we play with the blocks again after lunch, Mom?" Lily asked.

"Sure, sweetie," Mom said. "But only if you promise to listen to me next time. And maybe we can find a way to keep the cat away from your castle."

Lily and Ben promised. They thanked Mom for the lunch and gave her a kiss. They learned their lesson. They loved their blocks and their cat, but they loved their Mom more.

"Oh no, it's a flood!" Sara cried. "We have to fix it!"

Ben looked around and saw a big wrench on the floor. He picked it up and tried to turn the faucet, but it was too tight. He pushed harder and harder, but nothing happened. The water kept coming out and made a big puddle on the floor.

"Ben, stop! You're making it worse!" Sara said. "We have to get mom!"

"What do we do now?" Ben asked.

Sara thought for a moment and had an idea. She ran to the closet and got a big bucket. She brought it to the kitchen and put it under the sink. She said to Ben, "Help me fill the bucket with water. Then we can dump it outside."

Ben nodded and helped Sara. They worked together and filled the bucket with water. Then they carried it to the door and dumped it outside. They did this over and over again, until the water stopped coming out of the sink.

Lily felt sad. She liked the vest. It was soft and warm. She wanted to keep it. "No, Ben, the vest is nice. It was grandpa's. He gave it to me," she said.

"No, he did not. He gave it to me. I am a boy. Boys wear vests. Girls do not," Ben said. He grabbed the vest and tried to pull it off Lily.

"Stop, Ben, you are hurting me!" Lily cried. She held on to the vest and did not let go.

They both pulled and tugged and shouted. The vest ripped in half. The buttons and pockets fell off. The stuffing came out.

They looked at the vest. It was ruined. They felt bad. They had broken grandpa's vest. They had been mean to each other.

They heard a voice behind them. It was their mom. She had heard the noise and came to see what was wrong.

"What happened here?" she asked. She saw the vest and the mess. She was not happy.

"Lily and Ben, you have been naughty. You have fought over a vest that was not yours. You have wasted and spoiled a gift from grandpa. You have hurt each other's feelings. You should be sorry and say sorry," she said.

Lily and Ben knew their mom was right. They felt sorry. They said sorry to each other and hugged. They said sorry to their mom and helped her clean up. They said sorry to grandpa and promised to be good.

They learned a lesson. They learned to share and care. They learned to respect and value. They learned to love and forgive. They learned that a vest is not just a vest. It is a memory and a treasure.

One day, Tom and Lily went to the park with their mom. They liked to play on the swings, the slide and the seesaw. But they also liked to explore the park and look for animals and flowers.

"Can we go to the bush, mom?" Tom asked. He pointed to a big green bush near the fence. He thought he saw something move inside.

"Okay, but be careful. Don't go too far and don't touch anything sharp or dirty," mom said. She sat on a bench and watched them.

Tom and Lily ran to the bush and peeked inside. They saw a small brown animal with a long tail and big ears. It looked like a mouse, but bigger.

"Wow, look at that!" Lily said. "What is it?"

"I don't know. Maybe a rat," Tom said. He wanted to touch it, but he was a little scared.

"Hello, rat," Lily said. She smiled and waved at the animal.

The animal did not smile or wave back. It made a loud noise and showed its teeth. It looked very bad and angry.

"Ah, run!" Tom shouted. He grabbed Lily's hand and ran away from the bush.

The animal chased them for a few steps, then stopped and went back to the bush. It did not like to be disturbed.

Tom and Lily ran to their mom and hugged her. They were very scared and out of breath.

"What happened?" mom asked. She saw the animal in the bush and frowned.

"There was a bad rat in the bush. It tried to bite us," Tom said.

"Oh, no. That was not a rat. That was a possum. They are not bad, but they are shy and scared of people. You should not bother them," mom said.

"What is a possum?" Lily asked.

"A possum is a kind of animal that lives in trees and bushes. They come out at night and eat fruits and nuts. They are not pets, they are wild," mom said.

"Can we see it again?" Tom asked.

"No, you should leave it alone. It wants to remain in the bush and be quiet. Maybe we can see other animals that are more friendly, like birds or squirrels," mom said.

"Okay, mom. We are sorry, possum. We will not bother you again," Tom and Lily said.

They walked away from the bush and looked for other things to see and do in the park. They had fun, but they also learned to respect the animals and their homes.

Tom and Anna like to play with blocks. They build towers with different colors and shapes. They see who can make the tallest tower without falling down.

"Look at my tower, Anna!" Tom says. "It is very high and strong. It has a red block on top."

Anna looks at Tom's tower. She thinks it is nice, but she wants to make a better one. She adds more blocks to her tower. She puts a yellow block on top.

"My tower is higher and prettier than yours, Tom!" Anna says. "It has a yellow block on top. Yellow is my favorite color."

Tom feels a little sad. He likes his tower, but he thinks Anna's tower is higher and prettier too. He wants to make his tower higher and prettier, but he has no more blocks.

He sees a big rock on the ground. He has an idea. He picks up the rock and puts it on top of his tower.

"Ha! Now my tower is the highest and the strongest, Anna!" Tom says. "It has a rock on top. Rocks are very hard and dependable. They do not break or fall."

Anna looks at Tom's tower. She sees the rock on top. She thinks it is not fair. Rocks are not blocks. They do not belong in a tower. She feels angry.

She pushes Tom's tower with her hand. The rock falls off and hits the ground with a loud thud. The blocks fall down too. Tom's tower is gone.

"Hey! That is not nice, Anna!" Tom says. "You broke my tower. You are a meanie."

Anna feels sorry. She did not mean to break Tom's tower. She just wanted to win. She sees Tom's sad face. She wants to make him happy.

"I am sorry, Tom. I did not mean to break your tower. You are not a meanie. You are my friend." Anna says. "Can we play together again? Can we share the blocks and the rock?"

Tom smiles. He is not sad anymore. He is happy. He likes Anna. She is his friend.

"Okay, Anna. I am sorry too. I did not mean to make you angry. You are not a meanie. You are my friend." Tom says. "Yes, we can play together again. We can share the blocks and the rock. We can make a new tower. A bigger and better tower. A tower for both of us."

Lily and Ben are playing in the park. They like to slide, swing and run. They see a big black dog. The dog is barking loud. Lily and Ben are scared.

"Let's go away!" Lily says to Ben. "The dog is angry!"

They rush to the gate. They want to escape. But the gate is locked. They cannot open it. They look for help. They see a man. The man is wearing a hat and a coat. He has a leash in his hand.

"Help us, please!" Ben shouts to the man. "The dog is chasing us!"

The man hears Ben. He sees the dog. He runs to the gate. He opens it. He calls the dog.

"Rex, come here!" The man says to the dog. "Don't scare the children!"

The dog stops barking. He runs to the man. He wags his tail. He is not angry. He is happy.

"Sorry, kids!" The man says to Lily and Ben. "Rex is not a bad dog. He just wants to play. He likes to chase things. He is very friendly."

Lily and Ben are not scared anymore. They see the dog is nice. They pet the dog. They say sorry to the man.

"Thank you for helping us!" Lily says to the man. "Can we play with Rex?"

"Sure, you can!" The man says to Lily. "But be careful. He is very fast and strong. He likes to jump and lick."

Lily and Ben laugh. They play with Rex. They have fun. They are not afraid of the big black dog.

Tom and Lily were twins who liked to play in the park. They had a big red ball that they threw to each other. One day, they saw a man with a guitar and a hat on a path near the swings. He was singing and playing for the people who walked by. He looked happy and friendly.

"Let's go see him!" Tom said to Lily. "Maybe he will let us touch his guitar."

"OK, but be careful. He might not like it if we bother him," Lily said.

They ran to the man and smiled. The man smiled back and said, "Hello, little ones. Do you like my music?"

"Yes, we do!" Tom and Lily said together. "Can we try your guitar?"

The man laughed and said, "Sure, why not? It's a harmless instrument. But you have to be gentle with it. It's very precious to me."

He handed them his guitar and showed them how to hold it and strum it. Tom and Lily felt the strings and the wood. They made some noises with it and giggled.

"Wow, this is fun!" Tom said.

"You're very good!" Lily said.

The man clapped and said, "You're natural performers! Maybe you can join me someday and we can make music together."

Tom and Lily nodded and said, "Yes, please!"

They gave the guitar back to the man and thanked him. He gave them each a candy and said, "You're very welcome. Come back anytime. I'm always here on this path."

Tom and Lily waved goodbye and ran back to their ball. They had a new friend and a new hobby. They were very happy.

One day, a big, mean dog came to the park. He saw Spot and growled. He wanted to take the ball from Spot. He ran towards Spot and barked loudly. Spot was scared and ran away. Anna and Ben were scared too. They did not know what to do.

"Go away, bad dog!" Anna shouted. She picked up a stick and waved it at the big dog. Ben ran to her side and helped her. They wanted to protect Spot. They loved Spot.

The big dog was confused. He did not expect the children to fight back. He stopped and looked at them. He saw their angry faces and their sticks. He decided he did not want the ball anymore. He turned and ran away.

Spot came back to Anna and Ben. He wagged his tail and licked their faces. He was happy and grateful. Anna and Ben hugged him and praised him. They were happy and relieved.

"Good job, Anna and Ben!" their mom said. She had seen everything from a bench. She was proud and impressed. She gave them a snack and a drink. She also gave Spot a treat. They all sat together and enjoyed the park. They were safe and happy.

They think the drum is more interesting now. They like to fill the drum with things. They have fun with the drum.

Lily and Tom were playing in the park with their ball. They liked to kick the ball to each other and run after it. Sometimes the ball went too far and they had to look for it in the grass or behind the trees.

One day, the ball went over the fence and into the road. Lily and Tom ran to the fence and saw a big truck coming. The truck hit the ball and made a loud noise. The ball flew up in the air and landed on the roof of a building.

"Oh no!" Lily said. "Our ball is gone!"

Lily followed him. She was scared of the ladder and the roof. She did not like being so high. She wanted to go back to the park.

"Tom, come down!" she called. "It's not safe here!"

Later that day, Timmy went to play with his friends. They were playing near a big tree. Timmy was climbing the tree when suddenly, he slipped and fell. He landed on a rock and hurt his head.

When Timmy's mom came to pick him up, she saw that he was bleeding and rushed him to the hospital. The doctors tried to help Timmy, but it was too late. Timmy had hit his head too hard and he passed away.

Timmy's mom was devastated. She wished she had made him study instead of letting him play. She knew that if Timmy had studied, he would have been safe at home and not climbing trees.

Once upon a time, there was a little duck. The duck was very thirsty. He looked around for some water, but all he could see was dry land. The duck walked and walked, hoping to find some water. Suddenly, he saw a big pond in the distance. The duck was so happy that he started to run towards the pond. But, he was not strong enough to reach the pond. He was sad and tired.

Just then, a friendly rabbit came along. The rabbit saw the little duck and asked him what was wrong. The duck told the rabbit that he was very thirsty and couldn't reach the pond. The rabbit said he could help. He picked up the little duck and carried him to the pond. The duck was so happy that he drank and drank until he was no longer thirsty.

But then, the rabbit accidentally knocked over a bucket and made a loud noise. A mean old farmer heard the noise and thought the rabbit was stealing from him. He put the rabbit in jail! The little duck was so sad that his new friend was gone. But, he remembered how the rabbit had helped him reach the pond, so he decided to help the rabbit escape from jail. Together, they made a plan and the little duck was able to reach the keys to unlock the jail cell. They ran away and lived happily ever after.

Mommy was compassionate. She understood how Sara felt. She said, "It's okay, Sara. The doctor is very nice and gentle. He will not hurt your baby. He will only help her. And you can come with me and watch. You can hold your baby's hand and talk to her. How does that sound?"

Sara thought for a moment. She wanted her baby doll to be well. She nodded and said, "Okay, mommy. Let's go to the doctor. But I will not let go of my baby."

Mommy hugged Sara and said, "That's very brave of you, Sara. You are a good mommy. Come on, let's go."

They took the baby doll to the doctor. The doctor was kind and smiled. He said, "Hello, Sara. Hello, baby. What's your baby's name?"

Sara said, "Her name is Lily. She is my best friend."

The doctor said, "Lily is a beautiful name. And she is a lucky baby to have you as her mommy. Now, let me see what I can do for her dress. It will only take a few minutes. You can sit here and watch. And you can rock her and sing to her if you want."

Sara did as the doctor said. She rocked her baby doll and sang to her softly. She held her hand and said, "It's okay, Lily. The doctor is helping you. You will be better soon. I love you."

The doctor finished sewing the dress. He said, "There you go, Lily. You are all fixed. You look lovely. And you are very brave. How do you feel?"

Sara said, "Thank you, doctor. You are very nice. Lily feels much better. And so do I."

The doctor said, "You're welcome, Sara. You are very sweet. And you are a wonderful mommy. I'm glad you and Lily are happy."

Mommy said, "Thank you, doctor. You are very compassionate. You made Sara and Lily feel safe and comfortable. We appreciate your help."

The doctor said, "It was my pleasure. I enjoy helping children and their toys. You have a lovely day."

Sara and mommy said goodbye to the doctor. They left with Lily in Sara's arms. Sara rocked her baby doll and smiled. She was happy. She had a good mommy and a good doctor. And she had the best baby doll in the world.

He picked up a crystal and put it in his pocket. Lily saw him and shook her head.

"No, Tom, you can't do that!" she said. "The crystals belong to the hill. They are part of nature. If you take them, you are hurting the hill and the animals and the plants. That is not nice."

Tom frowned. He liked the crystal and wanted to keep it. But he also loved his sister and did not want to make her sad. He thought for a moment and then took the crystal out of his pocket.

"You are right, Lily," he said. "I'm sorry. I should not take things that are not mine. I will put the crystal back where I found it."

After dinner, Timmy went back to his room to play with his toys. He pretended that the cars were racing on a smooth road and the trucks were carrying beef to the market. Timmy had so much fun that he didn't even notice when it was time for bed.

Once upon a time, there was an old cat named Fat. Fat was very lazy and loved to sleep all day. One day, Fat's friend Mouse came to visit. "Hi Fat, do you want to play with me?" asked Mouse. "No, I'm too old to play. I just want to sleep," replied Fat.

Mouse was sad and said, "But we always play together. Why the delay?" Fat thought for a moment and said, "You're right, Mouse. I shouldn't be so lazy. Let's play!" So, Fat and Mouse played together all day and had so much fun.

From that day on, Fat wasn't so lazy anymore. He realized that even though he was old, he could still have fun with his friends. And Mouse was happy that he got to play with his friend Fat again.

Once upon a time, there was a little rabbit named Bun-Bun. One day, Bun-Bun was hopping around in the forest when he saw a big hole in the ground. He hopped down into the hole and found himself underground.

Suddenly, he heard a harsh voice say, "Who are you and what are you doing here?" It was a mole who lived underground. Bun-Bun explained that he was just exploring and meant no harm.

The mole didn't believe Bun-Bun and they started to argue. "I don't like strangers in my home," said the mole. "You need to leave now." Bun-Bun tried to speak calmly and explain himself, but the mole wouldn't listen.

Finally, Bun-Bun had an idea. "I can help you dig tunnels faster," he said. The mole was impressed and agreed to let Bun-Bun stay. They worked together and became good friends. From then on, Bun-Bun visited the underground world often and they always spoke kindly to each other.

They feel sad and confused. They want to read the book, but they do not understand it.

They see a lady near them. She is a teach. She helps children learn new things. She smiles at them and walks over.

"Hello, Lily and Ben," she says. "I see you have a very nice book. Do you like it?"

"Yes, we like it," Lily says. "But we do not know the words. They are too hard for us."

The teach nods. She says, "I understand. This book is for older children. It has many big words and names. But you can still enjoy it. Do you want me to help you?"

"Yes, please," Ben says. "We want to learn."

The teach sits with them and opens the book. She points to the pictures and tells them what they are. She says the words and names slowly and clearly. She asks them questions and lets them answer. She makes the book fun and easy for them.

Lily and Ben listen and look. They learn many new things. They see animals and plants they have never seen before. They say the words and names with the teach. They feel happy and smart.

"Thank you, teach," Lily says. "You are very kind and helpful. You make the book good for us."

"You are very welcome, Lily and Ben," the teach says. "You are very curious and eager. You make the book fun for me."

They smile and hug the teach. They continue to read the book together. They discuss the pictures and the words. They enjoy the pink book.

The moral of the story is: If you do not understand something, do not give up. Ask for help and learn from others. You can discover new things and have fun.

She ran to her mom and told her what happened. Her mom hugged her and told her that it was an accident. She told her that caterpillars are living things that need to be treated gently. She told her that sometimes they need to be left alone. She told her that she could learn more about them by reading books or watching them from a distance.

Lily nodded and said she was sorry. She asked her mom if the caterpillar would be okay. Her mom said she did not know, but they could go back and see. They walked to the garden and looked for the caterpillar. They found it on the ground, still curled up.

But then, something amazing happened. The caterpillar started to move. It uncurled and stretched its body. It had changed. It was not green and fuzzy anymore. It was colorful and shiny. It had wings. It was a butterfly.

"Sara, Daisy is very old," her dad said. He knelt down next to Sara and Daisy. "She has been a good horse for a long time, but now she is tired and in pain. She needs to rest and be comfortable."

"Can we make her better?" Sara asked. She looked at her dad with big, wet eyes.

Her dad shook his head. He looked sad too. "No, honey, we can't. Sometimes, animals get too old and they have to leave us. But we can thank them for being our friends and say goodbye."

Sara didn't understand. She didn't want Daisy to leave. She wanted Daisy to be happy and run and play. She cried and hugged Daisy harder.

Her dad hugged Sara and Daisy too. He whispered something in Daisy's ear. Then he got up and went to get a blanket. He covered Daisy with the blanket and made her warm.

"Sara, do you want to say something to Daisy?" he asked.

Sara nodded. She wiped her tears and leaned close to Daisy's ear. She said, "Daisy, you are a lovely horse. You are my best friend. I love you very much. Thank you for being with me. Goodbye, Daisy."

Daisy opened her eyes and looked at Sara. She licked Sara's cheek and made a soft sound. Then she closed her eyes again and was still.

Sara smiled and kissed Daisy's nose. She felt sad, but also happy. She knew Daisy loved her too. She knew Daisy was comfortable and peaceful. She knew Daisy would always be in her heart.

Ben did as Lily said and lay down on the soft mattress. Lily put the stethoscope on his chest and listened. She made a serious face.

Ben giggled. He knew Lily was just pretending. He liked to play along.

"OK, Lily. How can I relax?"

But the bee did not go away. It smelled the water in the cups and thought it was nectar. It flew closer and closer to the tea set, buzzing loudly. Lily's friends saw the bee and screamed. They dropped their cups and ran away. Lily was alone with the bee and the tea set.

She did not know what to do. She wanted to save her tea set, but she did not want to get stung by the bee. She wished her grandma was there to help her. She remembered that her grandma told her once that bees liked flowers, not people. She looked around and saw some yellow flowers growing near the tree. She had an idea.

She picked up one of the flowers and waved it in front of the bee. The bee saw the flower and followed it. Lily led the bee away from the tea set and towards the other flowers. She threw the flower into the bunch and ran back to the tree. She grabbed her tea set and put it in her bag. She was happy that she saved her tea set and that the bee found a better snack. She decided to serve tea to her friends another day, when there were no bees around.

His aunt said, "They have to answer some questions and sign some papers. It's nothing to worry about, Tommy. They love you very much and they will come back soon."

Tommy nodded, but he still felt a little nervous. He wondered what kind of questions and papers they had to deal with. He hoped they would not be too hard or scary.

He decided to play with his toys to distract himself. He made his cars race on the floor, his trains chug on the tracks, and his planes fly in the air. He pretended he was a driver, a conductor, and a pilot. He had fun and forgot about his worries for a while.

But then he heard a loud noise outside. He looked out the window and saw a big truck with flashing lights and a siren. He saw some men in uniforms get out of the truck and run into a building across the street. He saw smoke and flames coming out of the windows. He felt his heart beat faster and his hands tremble. He was afraid of the fire and the noise.

He ran to his aunt and hugged her. He said, "Auntie, what's happening? Is there a fire? Are the people okay?"

His aunt hugged him back and said, "Don't be scared, Tommy. It's okay. The firemen are here to put out the fire and help the people. They are brave and strong. They will make everything safe again."

She took him to the couch and turned on the TV. She found a channel with cartoons and said, "Let's watch something funny and happy, Tommy. How about this one? It's about a clever dog who solves mysteries with his friends."

Tommy nodded and snuggled with his aunt and his teddy bear. He watched the cartoon and smiled. He felt better and less afraid. He hoped his mom and dad would come back soon and tell him they were okay too. He hoped they would hug him and say they were proud of him for being so clever and brave.

Then she wanted to spread glue on the heart and sprinkle glitter on it. But the glue was too sticky and the glitter was too messy. She tried to squeeze the glue bottle, but it was hard. She tried to shake the glitter jar, but it spilled. She got glue and glitter on her hands, her clothes, her table and her floor. She was frustrated.

She started to cry. Her dad heard her and came to see what was wrong. He saw the mess and said, "Oh, Lily, what happened?" Lily sobbed, "I wanted to make a card for mom, but I can't. The glue and the glitter are bad. They don't work. They make a mess."

Her dad hugged her and said, "It's okay, Lily. You can still make a card for mom. You just need to do a test first. A test is when you try something small before you do something big. Let me show you." He took a small piece of paper and a crayon. He drew a dot and said, "This is a test. I want to see how much glue I need. I squeeze the bottle a little bit and put a drop of glue on the dot. See? That's enough. If I squeeze too much, the glue will run and make a mess. Now I take a pinch of glitter and sprinkle it on the glue. See? That's enough. If I shake too much, the glitter will fly and make a mess. Now I have a shiny dot. Do you want to try?"

Lily nodded and wiped her tears. She took another piece of paper and a crayon. She drew a star and said, "This is a test. I want to see how much glue and glitter I need." She followed her dad's instructions and made a shiny star. She smiled and said, "I did it! It's pretty. Can I do more?"

Her dad smiled and said, "Yes, you can. But first, let's clean up the mess. We don't want mom to see it. We want to surprise her with your card." They worked together to wipe the glue and glitter from the table, the floor, the clothes and the hands. Then they took the paper with the heart and the paper with the star. They glued the star on the heart and made a beautiful card. Lily was happy. She said, "Thank you, dad. You helped me. Mom will love it."

Her dad said, "You're welcome, Lily. You did a great job. I'm proud of you. And I'm sure mom will love it too. She loves you very much. And so do I." He kissed her and hugged her. They waited for mom to come home and gave her the card. Mom was surprised and delighted. She said, "Wow, Lily, this is a wonderful card. Thank you so much. I love you too." She kissed her and hugged her. Lily felt happy. She learned how to spread glue and glitter. She learned how to do a test. She learned how to make a card. And she learned how to make her mom smile.

Once there was a restless child. She was always looking for something to do. Her home never seemed to be enough.

One day, she found a big tree in a nearby park. And so she decided to try something she had never done before - she decided to hang from the tree. She wrapped her arms around the trunk of the tree and held on tight.

At first, everything was going well. But as the minutes went by, she started to feel very tired. She tried to swing a bit, but soon gave up.

Meanwhile, her parents had noticed her absence. They called out for her, but she did not reply. Worried, they went searching for her and they eventually found her hanging from the big tree.

The parents quickly ran to her, calling out her name. But the child was too exhausted to reply.

The parents took her home, gently putting her in her bed. She had learned her lesson about being so restless. From then on, she always find something entertaining to do around the house.

"Welcome, little fisherman! I am here to help. Don't be scared, I will take you safely home."

The fisherman was very thankful and the storm started calming down. Soon the sun came out and the sea became peaceful again. The voice was right, it became a beautiful day again and the fisherman was welcomed back home.

So, Timmy took the trophy home and put it on his shelf. But the trophy was smelly and made Timmy's room stink. Timmy didn't like that. 

The next day, Timmy's friend came to his house and asked for the trophy back. Timmy didn't want to give it back, but his friend got angry and took it away. Timmy was sad and learned that sometimes things that seem cool can cause problems.

Days went by and the little bird started to feel better. It was happy and chirping all the time. The moral of the story is that we should always try to help others, but sometimes things don't work out the way we want them to. It's important to accept that and move on, knowing that we did our best to help.

Once upon a time, there was a clumsy lizard named Liz. Liz loved to climb trees and eat bugs. One day, Liz climbed a tall tree and saw a big, shiny sack. 

Liz said, "What is in the sack?" 

A voice from inside the sack said, "None of your business, lizard!" 

Liz didn't listen and tried to open the sack. But Liz was too clumsy and knocked the sack down from the tree. 

The sack opened and out came a mean, old man. The man was very angry at Liz and said, "You ruined my plan, you silly lizard!" 

The man took Liz away and put her in a cage. Liz was very sad and missed her home in the tree. From that day on, Liz learned to listen and not be so curious.

When she got home, Mabel opened the box. She spread the cloth out on the ground and sprayed the lotion on. Then Mabel started to polish her favorite pink sneakers. She polished them until they sparkled.

The next day, Mabel went out to jog. She felt so fast and light in her special shiny shoes. Mabel smiled and shouted, "I'm the most graceful runner ever!"

Mabel kept polishing her shoes every day. Now when she went for a jog, Mabel glided gracefully across the ground. Everyone who saw her admired her beautiful, shiny shoes.

Billy was having so much fun. He didn't want the parade to ever end. He had the best time of his life.

Lily's mom took her to the hospital, where the doctor told her she had a concussion. From that day on, Lily always remembered to wear her helmet and never forgot that she needed a license to ride her bike on the road.

As they were packing up, Timmy's mom bought him an ice cream cone. Timmy was so happy and he ate it quickly. But then, he saw a seagull flying towards him. Timmy thought the seagull wanted his cone, so he tried to run away. But the seagull was too powerful and took the cone from Timmy's hand. Timmy was sad, but his mom promised they would get him another cone on the way home. And they did!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to cook with her mommy, especially in their big pot. They made great soup together.

One day, Lily's mommy went to the store and left the pot on the stove. Lily wanted to be like her mommy and cook, so she turned on the stove. But she forgot to put water in the pot. The pot got very hot and started to smoke.

When Lily's mommy came home, she saw the pot and said, "Oh no! Lily, what happened?" Lily started to weep and said, "I wanted to cook like you." But her mommy said, "It's okay, Lily. We can get a new pot. The important thing is that you're safe."

But when they went to buy a new pot, they saw that they didn't have enough money. Lily's mommy started to weep too. They couldn't make soup anymore, and it made them both very sad. The end.

She took him to the doctor who said it was just a flexible bone and nothing to worry about. Timmy was happy to hear that he was okay and went back to playing with his toys. 

As Timmy grew older, he loved to play sports. He found that being flexible helped him run faster and jump higher. He loved to show off his skills to his friends. One day, while playing basketball, Timmy fell and hurt his chest. His mommy took him to the doctor who said he just needed to rest and be fed lots of healthy food to help him heal. Timmy was happy to be taken care of and soon he was back to playing with his friends again. 

From then on, Timmy knew that being flexible was important for playing sports and that his mommy would always be there to feed him when he needed it. Timmy was grateful for his mommy's love and care.

Lily asked, "What do you need me to do, Grandma?"

Grandma replied, "Can you help me put my clothes in my luggage? I don't want them to freeze on the plane."

Suddenly, Lily said, "Grandma, I'm cold! Can we freeze too?"

Grandma laughed and said, "No, Lily, we can't freeze. But we can have fun on our trip together!"

Once upon a time, there was a big desert with no water. But in the middle of the desert, there was an oasis. It was a very special place with lots of green trees and a big pond of water. The animals loved to come to the oasis to drink and play. 

One day, a very busy ant came to the oasis. She was in a hurry to get back to her colony, but she stopped to rest for a minute. While she was there, she saw a wise old turtle. The turtle taught her about the importance of taking breaks and enjoying life. 

The ant listened carefully and promised to come back to the oasis more often. But she was so busy with work that she never made it back. She worked so hard that she became tired and thirsty. She searched and searched for water, but there was none to be found. She wished she had remembered the turtle's lesson and taken a break at the oasis. 

And so, the ant sadly perished in the hot desert, wishing she had taken the time to rest and learn from the wise turtle.

Later that day, Lily was playing her flute when she accidentally knocked over the vase. It fell to the ground and shattered into a million pieces. "Oh no, I'm so sorry!" cried Lily. "It's okay, sweetie. We can always buy a new one," said her mom, giving her a hug.

Timmy's mom saw him crying and asked him what was wrong. Timmy told her he wanted to catch the lime, but it was not a butterfly. His mom told him it was okay and that they could go to the store to buy some real butterflies to catch.

Timmy disagreed, "No, I want it to be big and have a basketball on it."

Timmy and Sally agreed and were happy with their trophies. They learned that it's okay to have different ideas and that compromising can lead to a good outcome.

Tim and Jen are friends. They like to play in the park. The park has a big slide, a swing, and a pond. The pond has fish and ducks.

One day, Tim and Jen go to the park in spring. The sun is bright and the sky is clear. They see the fish and the ducks in the pond. They want to feed them.

"Look, Jen, I have some bread for the fish and the ducks. Do you want some?" Tim says.

"Yes, please, Tim. Thank you. They must be hungry," Jen says.

They break the bread into small pieces and throw them into the pond. The fish and the ducks swim to the bread and eat them. Tim and Jen are happy.

But then, a big dog comes to the pond. The dog is black and furry. He has a long tail and sharp teeth. He sees the bread and the fish and the ducks. He wants them too.

He barks and runs to the pond. He scares the fish and the ducks. He jumps into the pond and splashes the water. He tries to catch the bread and the fish and the ducks.

"Stop, dog, stop! You are bad! You make the fish and the ducks suffer! Go away!" Tim shouts.

"Leave them alone, dog! You are mean! You make the water dirty! Go home!" Jen shouts.

But the dog does not listen. He keeps barking and running and jumping and splashing. He makes a big mess.

Tim and Jen are sad and angry. They want the dog to stop. They want the fish and the ducks to be safe. They want the pond to be clear.

They look for help. They see a man with a leash. The man is the dog's owner. He is looking for the dog.

"Sir, sir, please come! Your dog is bad! He makes the fish and the ducks suffer! He makes the pond dirty! Please take him away!" Tim and Jen say.

The man hears them. He sees the dog. He is sorry and ashamed.

"Oh, no, I'm so sorry. He ran away from me. He is naughty. Come here, boy, come here!" The man says.

He runs to the pond. He calls the dog. He puts the leash on the dog. He pulls the dog out of the pond.

"I'm very sorry, kids. He didn't mean to hurt the fish and the ducks. He was just curious and playful. He won't do it again. I'll take him home and teach him to behave. Please forgive him," The man says.

Tim and Jen are still sad and angry. But they are also kind and forgiving.

"It's okay, sir. We forgive him. But please don't let him do it again. The fish and the ducks are our friends. The pond is our park. We want them to be happy and clear," Tim and Jen say.

The man nods and smiles. He thanks them and apologizes again. He takes the dog away.

Tim and Jen look at the pond. The water is still dirty. The fish and the ducks are still scared. They feel sorry for them.

They decide to do something. They get some more bread. They throw it into the pond. They talk to the fish and the ducks.

"Sorry, fish, sorry, ducks. We didn't mean to make you suffer. We wanted to feed you. We hope you are okay. We hope you are not hurt. We hope you are still hungry. Here is some more bread. Please eat it. Please be happy," Tim and Jen say.

The fish and the ducks hear them. They see the bread. They are still scared. But they are also hungry and grateful.

They swim to the bread. They eat it. They quack and splash. They thank Tim and Jen.

Tim and Jen are happy. They see the fish and the ducks are happy. They hope the water will be clear soon.

They hug each other. They are friends. They love the park. They love the pond. They love the fish and the ducks. They love spring. They love the sun and the sky. They are happy.

"Wow, it's so pretty! I like its wings. They have many shapes and colors," Lily said.

"Really? That's amazing! How do they do that?" Lily asked.

"They are very creative. They use silk from their mouths to make the cocoon. Then they stay inside for a while and grow new parts. When they are ready, they break out of the cocoon and fly away," mom said.

"I want to see that! Can we find a caterpillar and a cocoon?" Tom asked.

"Maybe. But you have to be very quiet and listen. Sometimes you can hear the caterpillar munching on leaves or the butterfly coming out of the cocoon," mom said.

"Shh, I hear something. It sounds like a crack," Lily said.

"Me too. Maybe it's a butterfly coming out," Tom said.

"Wow, look, it's a butterfly!" Tom and Lily said.

"Yes, please!"

"Wow, Anna. You look like a real mermaid. You have a good haircut. Do you like it?"

"I love it. Thank you, Lisa. You are a good haircutter."

"You're welcome, Anna. You are a good imaginer."

"Good. Then you are my children and I am your father. I will always be with you and help you. I will never leave you nor forsake you. I will always love you," Jesus said.

The brothers started to fight. Sam wanted to use the microscope but Dan said it was his turn and he wouldn't let Sam have a go. Sam started to get angry and he pushed Dan out of the way - he wanted to prove that he was smart!

The museum staff decided to step in and stopped the brothers from fighting. But Sam was still determined to use the microscope. The museum staff then decided that the brothers could take turns in using the microscope.

At first, Dan was a little jealous that Sam got to use the microscope first. But when he had a go, he was amazed at what he saw. Looking through the microscope showed both brothers a whole new world they never knew existed before. They realised it was better to share and work together, than fight.

Once upon a time, there was a cute little bunny. He was always so careful and never part with caution. 
One day, the bunny was walking through the woods when he spotted a wolf. The wolf had a careless attitude, jumping and playing around. The bunny thought it was cute. 
The bunny asked the wolf, "Would you like to come and part with me?" 
The wolf answered, "Yes! I would love to part with you." 
The bunny and the wolf ran together, jumping and hopping over logs. They were having a great time. 
But then, suddenly the wolf stopped, and looked at the bunny slyly. The bunny then realised that the wolf was not being so careless after all. 
He had tricked the bunny, and he was ready to eat him!
The bunny was scared, but he knew he needed to act fast. He thought carefully, and then he quickly hopped up a nearby tree before the wolf could catch him. 
The wolf growled in frustration and stalked away, disappointed.
The bunny was safe and he realised that he had learned an important lesson - it's always important to be careful and not part with caution, especially with strange creatures that you don't know.

At first it was just a faint whisper, but as more and more time passed, the sound got louder and louder. As it grew, it took a rhythm that made the people feel scared. The animals shivered and hid.

But then something remarkable happened. The sun started to rise. And as the sun rose, the sound that was calling changed. The rhythm of the sound became softer and weaker until it was completely gone.

The people and animals thanked the sun for making everything ok again. They realized that the sound was only a distant echo that had been bouncing off the moon.

The tall clown heard the noise from outside and he was very angry. He rushed outside and saw the little child. He shouted at the child, "You can never unlock the door!" The poor child was too scared and started to cry.
The tall clown felt sorry for the child and he spoke in a soft voice. He said, "It's ok, I will forgive you this time. You can never unlock this door again!" The tall clown took the key and went back inside.

The little child was sad that the tall clown had gone. He never got a chance to meet him and he was too scared to ever come back. The tall clown lived happily in his palace, with all the doors and windows locked forever.

When it was time for bed, the child grabbed the dictionary and placed it on her nightstand. She smiled and said to herself, "This dictionary is mine and no one can take it away."

The child kept the dictionary forever. She soon began to learn the meanings of new words and even wrote out her own stories. The gray dictionary became her best friend and she accepted it with all her heart.

Once there was a family of four who lived in a big house. Every day they would have breakfast together. On this day, the dad was holding a big photo of the family. He looked at the photo and said, "Let's all go for a walk today!" 

The whole family agreed and put on their shoes. As they stepped out of the house, the dad placed the photo in his pocket.

"Why did you put the photo in your pocket, dad?" his 3 year old daughter asked.

Dad smiled and said gently, "I want to take it with us, so we can take a photo together. It will be a nice reminder of today!"

The family smiled and continued their walk. They held hands, laughed and enjoyed the day.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lucy. She was a very curious little girl and one day she told her mum she wanted to go to the zoo. Her mum said yes and the next day, Lucy was ready for an adventure.

At the zoo, Lucy saw lots of animals. Big animals and small animals, funny animals and some that were very scary. But Lucy was brave and she enjoyed looking at them all. She saw many pretty birds and butterflies.

 Lucy was so excited that it made her very tired. After she had seen all the animals, she went to sleep in her mum's arms. She was so cozy and it felt very nice.

When Lucy woke up, it was time to go home. She had so much fun at the zoo that she wanted to go back again. But for now, she was happy to go back home and sleep in her own bed.

Once upon a time, there was a furry little boat. It was so cute, with bright blue eyes and a big smile. One day, the boat decided to sail off into the big blue sea.

As the boat sailed along, it looked up at the big blue sky. It saw some fluffy white clouds and some little birds flying through the air. It was a beautiful sight!

The boat sailed further and further, until it reached a big island. On the island was a theater and a movie was playing inside. It was a funny film about a group of animals and their adventures. The boat was so excited because it wanted to watch the film too.

So, it sailed into the theater and curled up in the back row. It watched the movie with a big smile on its face. When the movie ended, the boat was sad to leave but it was also very happy because it had seen such a great film.

The boat sailed off back across the big blue sea, with the movie in its mind. It was glad it had gone sailing and had seen such a nice film.

Anna liked to sort her bricks by color. She had red bricks, blue bricks, yellow bricks and green bricks. She made piles of each color on the floor of her room. She felt peaceful when she sorted her bricks. She liked how they looked and how they fit together.

One day, her brother Ben came into her room. He saw her bricks and wanted to play with them. He grabbed some of the bricks from each pile and threw them in the air. He laughed and said, "Look, Anna, bricks can fly!"

Anna was not happy. She did not like how Ben messed up her bricks. She did not like how he made noise and broke her peace. She said, "No, Ben, bricks cannot fly. Bricks are for sorting and building. Please give me back my bricks and go away."

Ben did not listen. He kept throwing bricks and laughing. He said, "Bricks are fun. Bricks are for flying and crashing. You are boring, Anna. You do not know how to play."

Anna was very angry. She did not want to share her bricks with Ben. She did not want to play with him. She wanted him to leave her alone. She shouted, "Stop it, Ben! Stop throwing my bricks! You are mean and rude. You are not my friend."

Their mom heard them shouting and came into the room. She saw the bricks all over the floor and the children fighting. She was not pleased. She said, "What is going on here? Why are you making such a mess and such a noise? Why are you not getting along?"

Anna and Ben both tried to explain. Anna said, "Ben took my bricks and threw them. He ruined my sorting and my peace. He is bad." Ben said, "Anna was boring and selfish. She did not let me play with her bricks. She is mean."

Their mom shook her head. She said, "You are both wrong. Bricks are for sharing and playing nicely. You can sort them, you can fly them, you can build with them, but you have to respect each other and your things. You have to say please and thank you and sorry. You have to be kind and gentle and quiet. You have to be friends."

Anna and Ben looked at each other. They felt sorry for what they did. They said, "We are sorry, mom. We are sorry, Anna. We are sorry, Ben." They hugged each other and their mom. They said, "We will share and play nicely. We will respect each other and our bricks. We will be kind and gentle and quiet. We will be friends."

Their mom smiled. She said, "That's good. I'm glad you learned your lesson. Now, let's clean up this mess and then you can play with your bricks together. Maybe you can sort them by color and then make a big castle or a rocket or a bridge. What do you think?"

Anna and Ben nodded. They said, "Yes, mom. That sounds fun. We think that's a good idea." They picked up their bricks and put them back in their piles. They felt peaceful and happy. They thanked their mom and said, "We love you, mom. We love you, Anna. We love you, Ben." They started to play with their bricks together. They sorted them, they flew them, they built with them. They were friends.

Lily and Lila are twins. They like to perform for their mom and dad. They sing songs, dance, and tell jokes. They have a lot of fun.

One day, they decide to perform a race. They put on their shoes and go to the backyard. They draw a line with a stick. They say, "Ready, set, go!" and run as fast as they can.

Lily is very fast. She runs ahead of Lila. She thinks she will win. She looks back and smiles. But she does not see the rock. She trips and falls. She hurts her knee. She cries.

Lila sees Lily fall. She stops running. She runs to Lily. She hugs her and says, "Are you okay, Lily? I'm sorry you fell. You are very fast. You are a good runner."

Lily stops crying. She hugs Lila and says, "Thank you, Lila. You are very kind. You are a good sister. I love you."

Mom and dad see the twins. They come to the backyard. They say, "We are proud of you, Lily and Lila. You are good performers. You are good racers. But most of all, you are good friends." They kiss the twins and take them inside. They give them cookies and milk. The twins are happy.

Lily and Max were playing in the living room. They liked to pretend they were kings and queens in a fancy castle. They wore crowns and capes and sat on big chairs. They had a fireplace that made the room warm and cozy.

"Max, I want to see the fire," Lily said. "Can we go closer?"

"Okay, but be careful," Max said. "Fire is hot and can hurt you. We need to use a stick to poke it."

They got up and walked to the fireplace. Max picked up a long stick that was next to the wood. He reached out and poked the fire with the stick. The fire made a crackling sound and sparks flew.

"Wow, look at that!" Lily said. "The fire is so bright and pretty."

She wanted to try it too. She grabbed another stick and tried to strike the fire with it. But she was too small and clumsy. She missed the fire and hit the wall instead. The stick bounced back and hit her on the head.

"Ow!" Lily cried. "That hurt!"

Max dropped his stick and ran to her. He hugged her and said, "I'm sorry, Lily. Are you okay?"

Lily rubbed her head and nodded. She felt a bump on her forehead. She was not happy.

"Let's not play with the fire anymore," she said. "It's too dangerous."

"Okay," Max said. "Let's go back to our chairs and have some tea. We can still be kings and queens."

They left the sticks and the fire alone. They went back to their chairs and pretended to sip tea from their cups. They smiled and talked about their fancy castle. They forgot about the bump and the fire. They were happy again.

Lily and Ben were best friends. They liked to play in the park every day. They liked to swing, slide and run. But their favorite thing was to jump on the spring.

The spring was a big metal coil that was stuck in the ground. It had a seat on top that you could sit on and bounce up and down. Lily and Ben loved to bounce on the spring and pretend they were flying.

"Tom," he said in a low voice.

"I can't," Tom said. "I broke my leg and it hurts. I can't run or jump or do anything fun."

Lily and Ben felt sorry for Tom. They wanted to help him.

"We have an idea," Lily said. "You can bounce on the spring with us. It's very fun and it doesn't hurt your leg."

"How can I bounce on the spring with a broken leg?" Tom asked.

"We will support you," Ben said. "We will hold your hands and help you sit on the seat. Then we will bounce together and you will feel like you are flying."

Tom thought that sounded unusual, but also exciting. He agreed to try it. Lily and Ben supported him and helped him sit on the spring. Then they bounced up and down, gently and slowly. Tom felt the wind in his hair and the sun on his face. He smiled and laughed.

"Thank you, Lily and Ben," he said. "You are very kind and you made me happy. Can we be friends?"

"Of course," Lily and Ben said. "We are always happy to make new friends. And we can bounce on the spring together every day."

"Can I see it?" Lila asked, reaching for it.

"Sure, here you go," Ben said, giving it to her.

Lila felt the iron in her hand. It was cold and heavy. She wondered what it tasted like. She put it in her mouth and tried to chew it.

"Ow, ow, ow!" Lila cried, spitting it out. "Iron is bad! It hurts my teeth!"

Ben looked at her, shocked. "Lila, why did you chew the iron? You can't chew iron! It is not food! It is metal!"

"I wanted to try it. I didn't know it was bad. I'm sorry, Ben," Lila said, rubbing her mouth.

"It's okay, Lila. I'm sorry you hurt your teeth. Here, have some water. And don't chew iron again, okay?" Ben said, handing her a cup.

"Okay, Ben. Thank you. And don't chew iron either, okay?" Lila said, taking a sip.

"Okay, Lila. I won't. Let's go find something else to play with. Something soft and nice," Ben said, putting the iron away.

One day, he saw a big school of fish near the shore. He said to his friend Sam, who was also a fisherman, "Let's go catch those fish. They look tasty and fat. We can sell them at the market and get a lot of money."

Sam agreed and they got on their boats. They drove fast to the fish and threw their nets in the water. They pulled the nets and saw many fish inside. They were happy and smiled.

But then, they heard a roar. It was a big shark. The shark smelled the fish and wanted to eat them. He swam towards the boats and opened his mouth. He bit the nets and tore them apart. The fish escaped and the shark chased them.

Tom and Sam were scared and angry. They said to each other, "Oh no! The shark ruined our plan. He took our fish. He is mean and greedy. What can we do?"

Tom thought hard. He had an idea. He said to Sam, "I have a plan. Let's use the horn to trick the shark. We can make him go away and save our fish."

Sam asked, "How can we do that?"

Tom said, "We can make the horn sound like a bigger shark. The shark will think there is another shark here and he will be afraid. He will run away and leave us alone."

Sam said, "That is a clever plan. Let's try it."

They turned on the horn and made it sound like a bigger shark. They made it loud and scary. The shark heard the horn and stopped. He looked around and saw no other shark. He was confused and curious. He swam closer to the boats and the horn.

Tom and Sam waited for the right moment. When the shark was near the horn, they turned it off and shouted, "Boo!"

The shark was surprised and frightened. He thought the boats and the horn were a bigger shark. He turned around and swam away as fast as he could. He did not come back.

Tom and Sam cheered and clapped. They said to each other, "We did it! We scared the shark away. We are clever fishermen. We can catch our fish again."

Tom was a prince who liked to play with his toys. He had many toys, but his favorite was a magic wand that could make things shrink or grow. He liked to shrink his toy soldiers and make them march on his table, or grow his toy dragon and make it roar.

One day, he was playing with his wand when he saw his sister Lily. Lily was a princess who liked to read books and draw pictures. She had a big book that she was reading in the garden. Tom thought it would be fun to shrink her book and make her look for it.

He pointed his wand at the book and said, "Shrink!" The book became very small and fell on the grass. Lily looked up and saw Tom with his wand. She was angry and sad. She said, "Tom, what did you do? That was my book! It was a gift from Mom and Dad! Give it back!"

Tom felt guilty. He knew he had done something bad. He wanted to say sorry, but he was afraid. He ran away with his wand and hid in his room.

Lily searched for her book, but she could not find it. She cried and cried. She went to Mom and Dad and told them what Tom had done. Mom and Dad were disappointed and worried. They said, "Tom, come here. We need to talk to you."

Tom heard them and felt more guilty. He knew he had to face them and give back the book. He took his wand and went to the garden. He found the book on the grass and said, "Grow!" The book became big again and he picked it up. He saw Lily, Mom and Dad waiting for him. He walked to them and said, "I'm sorry. I was playing with my wand and I shrunk your book. It was a bad thing to do. Here is your book. Please forgive me."

Lily took her book and hugged it. She was happy to have it back. She looked at Tom and said, "Thank you for giving back my book. I forgive you. But don't do that again. It's not nice to shrink other people's things."

Mom and Dad nodded and said, "We're glad you said sorry and fixed your mistake. But you have to be careful with your wand. It's a powerful toy and you have to use it wisely. Don't use it to hurt or annoy others. Use it to have fun and be creative."

Tom nodded and said, "I understand. I'm sorry. I love you all." He hugged them and said, "Can we still play together?"

Lily smiled and said, "Yes, we can. But let's play with something else. How about we draw some pictures?"

Tom agreed and said, "Okay, let's do that. But can I keep my wand?"

Lily said, "Only if you promise to be good."

Tom said, "I promise. I'll be good."

They went to the house and got some paper and crayons. They drew some pictures of their toys and their family. They had fun and forgot about the wand. They were happy.

Sandy had finally accomplished her goal of touching all the toys. She was happy and relieved to have her dad's help and she was proud of herself. From that moment on, Sandy made sure that she always asked for help when she was faced with a difficult task.

One day, Sammy was walking in the woods when he saw a note. He picked up the small note and read it. The note said, "Fight if you want to learn more!" Sammy was excited. He wanted to learn more so he decided to fight.

Sammy went to the big tree and saw two animals. It was a cat and a mouse. They were fighting! Sammy watched them for a while. He wanted to join in, but he was too small. He wasn't sure if he should fight.

The cat and mouse saw Sammy and started to laugh. They told Sammy he was too small to fight. Sammy was sad. He wanted to learn more, but he was too small.

Suddenly, Sammy felt brave. He ran towards the cat and mouse and shouted, "I can fight too!" Sammy was small, but he was brave. The cat and mouse stopped fighting and looked at Sammy in surprise. Sammy was brave and he learned a lot that day.

One day, Jill found a magic wand. She waved it around the armchair and around the room. Then, just like in the stories she read, the room filled with sparkles and the armchair changed. 

The armchair became very big. It was so big that Jill could hide inside of it. She was amazed. She tried to climb inside, but she was too small. She needed to use the magic wand. She waved it one more time and the armchair started to shrink until it was just the right size for her.

Jill sat in the armchair and it was so comfortable and cozy. She was happy that she had made it yield to her wishes. From that day on, her armchair was the best seat in the house.

The child went up to the robot and said "Can you play with me?" But the robot was too tired to even answer.

So the child grabbed a cloth and a bucket of water. She started cleaning like the robot was doing. She cleaned the floors, the windows and the walls.

The robot was so happy to see the child. He said "Good job cleaning! Now I can take a rest."

The child and the robot were happy and the small robot thanked the child for helping him clean.

Suddenly, he heard a noise. He looked up and saw that it was a broken kite. He wondered what had happened to it. He wanted to find out, but then he realised that it was too high up. He couldn't get to it.

The bug was sad. But then he heard a buzzing behind him. He turned around to see that there were lots of other insects flying and buzzing around the garden. He felt much better. He knew he wasn't alone. He waved goodbye to his insect friends and went back to exploring the garden.

The rabbit said, "You just need to accept yourself for who you are". The bear thought about this for a long time.

The next day, the bear was feeling better. He decided to try something new. He started to put salt on all his food! He had never done that before. It was a strange feeling, but he liked it.

Soon, the bear was feeling happy again. He accepted himself for who he was and accepted the new food choices he was making. He was no longer a sleepy bear. He was a happy and content bear.

Once upon a time there was a girl named Lucy. She was three years old and she had lots of friends. One day she thought it would be nice to make a surprise for them. She wanted to make something yummy and special. So she went to her mom's kitchen and found everything she needed.

Once she had all the ingredients ready, she started to mix them together. But she was so excited that she kept adding things without tasting them. When she was finished she thought it tasted good. But when she offered it to her friends, they said it was rude.

Lucy was so sad! She couldn't understand why nobody wanted to eat what she made. She tasted it again and realized it was a little too sweet. She tried adding some sour things, but it didn't seem to help. In the end she had to throw it all away. 

But Lucy still made a wonderful surprise for her friends. She decided to make a picture from all the colorful ingredients she used. Everyone was very happy and had lots of fun. From that day on Lucy always tasted her food first and everyone enjoyed her yummy surprises!

Once, there was a little girl named Sarah who was 3 years old. She was walking through the dark woods and, as she went along, she started to feel scared and her body began to tremble.

She kept walking and eventually came upon a bowl filled with something in the middle of the woods. She could not tell what it was, but it was dark, so she was afraid. She was so scared that her arms and legs were shaking.

Sarah did not want to look in the bowl, but something made her do it. She slowly leaned over and peered into the bowl. To her surprise, it was filled with a beautiful red rose!

Sarah was relieved and happily picked up the rose. She knew it would make a great gift for her mommy. She thanked the bowl and happily started walking back home. She was not scared anymore and skipped along with the rose in her hand.

Once upon a time, there was a grumpy man who was always mad. He was always yelling and even frowned a lot.

One day, the grumpy man went to the store and bought something he didn't need. The cashier asked him to pay, but he did not have enough money in his wallet. The cashier said the man must pay or else he would be punished.

This made the grumpy man even madder. He growled and crossed his arms. The cashier said he would have to call the police if he didn't pay for what he bought.

After a few moments of thinking, the grumpy man opened his wallet and paid for the item. The cashier thanked him, and the man left the store grumpily.

The grumpy man had learned his lesson. He knew that if he didn't pay for what he bought he would be punished.
